meta.derivedFrom: J. Barton Payne, Encyclopedia of Biblical Prophecy (Messianic subset)

prophecies.title: Seed of the Woman
prophecies.otText: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.
prophecies.otTextZh: 我又要叫你和女人彼此为仇；你的后裔和女人的后裔也彼此为仇。女人的后裔要伤你的头；你要伤他的脚跟。
prophecies.ntText: The one who does what is sinful is of the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the beginning. The reason the Son of God appeared was to destroy the devil's work.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 犯罪的是属魔鬼，因为魔鬼从起初就犯罪。神的儿子显现出来，为要除灭魔鬼的作为。
prophecies.explanation: From the very first pages of Genesis, God promised that a descendant of the woman would one day crush the serpent's head. 1 John reveals that Jesus is that promised offspring—the Son of God who appeared to destroy the devil's work. The battle between good and evil was not an afterthought; it was addressed in God's very first promise of redemption.
prophecies.explanationZh: 创世记一开始，上帝就应许女人的后裔终将伤蛇的头。约翰一书表明耶稣就是那应许的后裔——神的儿子显现为要除灭魔鬼的作为。善恶之争并非事后才想到，它早已在上帝救赎的第一步应许中宣告。

interpretations.note: Seed of woman crushing serpent; Payne treats this as foundational messianic promise opening all redemptive history
Paraphrased with express reference to the Messiah in Targum Pseudo-Jonathan; the seed crushing the serpent's head applied to Messiah in multiple Midrashim

interpretations.title: Born of the Seed of Woman
interpretations.note: First Messianic promise; seed of woman crushes serpent — cited with Targum Jonathan

prophecies.title: Blessing Through Abraham
prophecies.otText: I will bless those who bless you, and whoever curses you I will curse; and all peoples on earth will be blessed through you.
prophecies.otTextZh: 为你祝福的，我必赐福与他；那咒诅你的，我必咒诅他。地上的万族都要因你得福。」
prophecies.ntText: The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. Scripture does not say "and to seeds," meaning many people, but "and to your seed," meaning one person, who is Christ.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 所应许的原是向亚伯拉罕和他子孙说的。神并不是说「众子孙」，指著许多人，乃是说「你那一个子孙」，指著一个人，就是基督。
prophecies.explanation: God's promise to Abraham was never just about one nation—it was about all peoples on earth being blessed. Paul explains in Galatians that this singular 'seed' is Christ himself. Through Jesus, the ancient blessing given to Abraham reaches every tribe, tongue, and nation.
prophecies.explanationZh: 上帝呼召亚伯拉罕并宣告万国必因他的后裔得福。保罗指出这「后裔」根本上指向基督，而非仅仅是众多子孙。福音书和使徒书信都见证，亚伯拉罕所领受的祝福在耶稣里临到万国。

interpretations.title: Seed of Abraham
interpretations.note: Galatians 3:16 — 'seed' singular; Matthew Henry cited on universal blessing through one descendant

prophecies.title: From the Tribe of Judah
prophecies.otText: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until he to whom it belongs shall come and the obedience of the nations shall be his.
prophecies.otTextZh: 圭必不离犹大，杖必不离他两脚之间，直等细罗来到，万民都必归顺。
prophecies.ntText: For it is clear that our Lord descended from Judah, and in regard to that tribe Moses said nothing about priests.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 我们的主分明是从犹大出来的；但这支派，摩西并没有提到祭司。
prophecies.explanation: Jacob's ancient blessing singled out Judah as the tribe from which the ultimate ruler would come. Hebrews confirms that Jesus descended from Judah—not from the priestly tribe of Levi—establishing that his authority comes not from the old priesthood but from a higher calling as both King and Priest.
prophecies.explanationZh: 雅各临终预言「圭必不离犹大」,表明君王要从犹大支派而出。弥赛亚的谱系不断收紧，最终指向大卫的后裔。耶稣的族谱确认他正是从犹大支派、大卫家出生的君王。

interpretations.note: Scepter not departing from Judah until Shiloh comes; ruler from Judah lineage narrowed to Christ
Extensively discussed; Shiloh applied directly to Messiah in Targum Pseudo-Jon. with full Rabbinic commentary in Sanh. 98b

interpretations.title: Tribe of Judah
interpretations.note: Scepter passage with Targum Jonathan cited verbatim; Hengstenberg commentary included

prophecies.title: Prophet Like Moses
prophecies.otText: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among you, from your fellow Israelites. You must listen to him. … I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their fellow Israelites, and I will put my words in his mouth. He will tell them everything I command him.
prophecies.otTextZh:
耶和华─你的神要从你们弟兄中间给你兴起一位先知，像我，你们要听从他。
正如你在何烈山大会的日子求耶和华─你神一切的话，说：『求你不再叫我听见耶和华─我神的声音，也不再叫我看见这大火，免得我死亡。』
耶和华就对我说：『他们所说的是。
我必在他们弟兄中间给他们兴起一位先知，像你。我要将当说的话传给他；他要将我一切所吩咐的都传给他们。
prophecies.ntText: For Moses said, 'The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you must listen to everything he tells you.' … After the people saw the sign Jesus performed, they began to say, 'Surely this is the Prophet who is to come into the world.'
prophecies.ntTextZh:
摩西曾说：『主─神要从你们弟兄中间给你们兴起一位先知像我，凡他向你们所说的，你们都要听从。
众人看见耶稣所行的神迹，就说：「这真是那要到世间来的先知！」
prophecies.explanation: Moses was the greatest prophet Israel had ever known—the one who spoke with God face to face. Yet Moses himself said another prophet would come, one in whom God would place His own words. Peter declared in Acts that Jesus is that prophet, the one all Israel was commanded to listen to. And when Jesus multiplied bread, the crowds recognized Him as the Prophet who was to come. Just as Moses delivered Israel from Egypt, Jesus delivers humanity from sin—the ultimate mediator between God and His people.
prophecies.explanationZh: 摩西预言上帝要兴起一位像他的先知，人们必须听从他。使徒行传和福音书都认定这应许指向基督。正如摩西带领以色列出埃及，基督要带领他的百姓脱离罪的捆绑并把律法写在心上。

interpretations.note: Prophet like Moses raised up; Payne notes Jewish expectation of a second Moses fulfilled in Christ

interpretations.title: Shall Be a Prophet
interpretations.note: Maimonides letter to Yemen cited; Kligerman on Jewish expectation of Messianic prophet

prophecies.title: The Passover Lamb
prophecies.otText: It must be eaten inside the house; take none of the meat outside the house. Do not break any of the bones.
prophecies.otTextZh: 应当在一个房子里吃；不可把一点肉从房子里带到外头去。羊羔的骨头一根也不可折断。
prophecies.ntText: These things happened so that the scripture would be fulfilled: "Not one of his bones will be broken."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 这些事成了，为要应验经上的话说：「他的骨头一根也不可折断。」
prophecies.explanation: The Passover lamb's bones were never to be broken—a detail that seemed minor until the crucifixion. When soldiers came to break the legs of those crucified, Jesus had already died, and not one of his bones was broken. John saw this as direct fulfillment: Jesus is the true Passover Lamb whose sacrifice delivers God's people from death.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以色列在埃及的逾越节所宰杀的羊羔，其血救了百姓免于灭命者的击杀。保罗明言「我们逾越节的羔羊基督已经被杀献祭了」。耶稣被钉十架的时间与方式都与逾越节羔羊呼应。

interpretations.note: Passover lamb typology connected to Messianic redemption in Talmudic sources

prophecies.title: Son of David
prophecies.otText: When your days are over and you rest with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring to succeed you, your own flesh and blood, and I will establish his kingdom.
prophecies.otTextZh: 你寿数满足、与你列祖同睡的时候，我必使你的后裔接续你的位；我也必坚定他的国。
prophecies.ntText: He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David,
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他要为大，称为至高者的儿子；主神要把他祖大卫的位给他。
prophecies.explanation: God made a covenant with David that his throne would be established forever. No earthly king could fulfill that promise—every dynasty eventually falls. The angel Gabriel announced to Mary that her son Jesus would receive David's throne, and his kingdom would have no end. Jesus is the eternal King that David's line always pointed toward.
prophecies.explanationZh: 上帝与大卫立约，应许他的后裔永远坐大卫的宝座。众先知反复确认弥赛亚作为大卫之子的身份。福音书以「大卫的子孙」称呼耶稣，证明他就是那约的应验。

interpretations.note: Davidic throne established forever; Payne treats as foundational covenant for all Davidic messianism

prophecies.title: Born of a Virgin
prophecies.otText: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and will call him Immanuel.
prophecies.otTextZh: 因此，主自己要给你们一个兆头，必有童女怀孕生子，给他起名叫以马内利（就是神与我们同在的意思）。
prophecies.ntText: "The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel" (which means "God with us").
prophecies.ntTextZh: 说：必有童女怀孕生子；人要称他的名为以马内利。（以马内利翻出来就是「神与我们同在」。）
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah promised a miraculous sign: a virgin would conceive and bear a son called Immanuel—'God with us.' Matthew saw this fulfilled in the birth of Jesus to the virgin Mary. This was not merely a remarkable birth; it was God entering the human story in the most intimate way possible, literally dwelling among his people.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言必有童女怀孕生子，名为以马内利（神与我们同在）。马太福音明确引用这预言，表明耶稣由童贞女马利亚所生。这指出弥赛亚并非普通君王，而是神的同在亲自临到人间。

interpretations.note: Virgin conceives Immanuel; Payne argues almah requires virgin, not merely young woman
Cited in Messianic context; sign applied to the Messianic era in Targum and Talmudic sources

interpretations.title: Born of a Virgin
interpretations.note: Greek LXX uses parthenos; Targum Isaiah cited; Immanuel also listed separately as #15

prophecies.title: Light in Galilee
prophecies.otText: Nevertheless, there will be no more gloom for those who were in distress. In the past he humbled the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but in the future he will honor Galilee of the nations, by the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan—The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of deep darkness a light has dawned.
prophecies.otTextZh:
但那受过痛苦的必不再见幽暗。从前神使西布伦地和拿弗他利地被藐视，末后却使这沿海的路，约旦河外，外邦人的加利利地得著荣耀。
在黑暗中行走的百姓看见了大光；住在死荫之地的人有光照耀他们。
prophecies.ntText: the people living in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death a light has dawned.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 那坐在黑暗里的百姓看见了大光；坐在死荫之地的人有光发现照著他们。
prophecies.explanation: Galilee was a region looked down upon—remote, mixed with Gentile populations, and historically humbled by foreign invaders. Yet Isaiah said this despised region would be the first to see a great light. When Jesus began his public ministry in Galilee, Matthew recognized the fulfillment: hope dawned first in the place least expected.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言在黑暗中的加利利地要看见大光。马太福音引证这正是耶稣在加利利展开服事的应验。那位大光就是基督——把福音带给外邦人与被辖制之民的光。

interpretations.note: Galilee region sees great light; Payne notes geographic specificity as confirming mark
Applied to Messianic times and the light of the Messiah in Yalkut and Talmud

interpretations.title: Ministry to Begin in Galilee
interpretations.note: Galilee of Gentiles illuminated; Capernaum as fulfillment — Matt 4:12 cited

prophecies.title: Messenger Before Messiah
prophecies.otText: "I will send my messenger, who will prepare the way before me. Then suddenly the Lord you are seeking will come to his temple; the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire, will come," says the LORD Almighty.
prophecies.otTextZh: 万军之耶和华说：「我要差遣我的使者在我前面预备道路。你们所寻求的主必忽然进入他的殿；立约的使者，就是你们所仰慕的，快要来到。」
prophecies.ntText: as it is written in Isaiah the prophet: "I will send my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way"—
prophecies.ntTextZh: 正如先知以赛亚（有古卷没有以赛亚三个字）书上记著说：看哪，我要差遣我的使者在你前面，预备道路。
prophecies.explanation: Malachi prophesied that a messenger would come to prepare the way for the Lord. Mark opens his Gospel by identifying John the Baptist as that messenger. Just as a herald goes before a king, John called Israel to repentance so that hearts would be ready to receive the Messiah when he arrived.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚和玛拉基都预言在弥赛亚之前要有一位预备道路的使者。施洗约翰就是那「在旷野呼喊」的声音，为耶稣预备人心。这一应验把旧约预言与新约事件直接相连。

interpretations.note: Messenger prepares the way; Payne identifies John the Baptist as direct fulfillment

interpretations.title: He Was to Enter the Temple
interpretations.note: Lord suddenly coming to His temple; John 1:14 and 2:19-21 cited as fulfillments

prophecies.title: Born in Bethlehem
prophecies.otText: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come for me one who will be ruler over Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient times.
prophecies.otTextZh: 伯利恒的以法他啊，你在犹大诸城中为小，将来必有一位从你那里出来，在以色列中为我作掌权的；他的根源从亘古，从太初就有。
prophecies.ntText: After Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, during the time of King Herod, Magi from the east came to Jerusalem
prophecies.ntTextZh: 当希律王的时候，耶稣生在犹太的伯利恒。有几个博士从东方来到耶路撒冷，说：
prophecies.explanation: Micah named the tiny village of Bethlehem as the birthplace of Israel's future ruler—one whose origins reach back to eternity. Matthew records that Jesus was indeed born in Bethlehem, in fulfillment of this prophecy. The eternal God chose the humblest of towns to enter the world, showing that his kingdom is built not on earthly grandeur but on divine purpose.
prophecies.explanationZh: 弥迦预言以色列的掌权者要从小城伯利恒出来。马太福音记载耶稣按此预言诞生于伯利恒。上帝藉着卑微小镇成就最伟大的救赎，证明应许精确地成就。

interpretations.note: Ruler from Bethlehem of ancient origins; Payne emphasizes eternal origin clause as divine
Bethlehem as Messiah's birthplace attested via Gen 35:21 in Targum Pseudo-Jon.; Mic 5:2 cited in Talmudic discussion of Messianic origin

interpretations.title: Born at Bethlehem
interpretations.note: Scribes cited in Matt 2:4; Hengstenberg commentary; pre-existence in same verse noted as #13

prophecies.title: King Priest
prophecies.otText: The LORD has sworn and will not change his mind: "You are a priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek."
prophecies.otTextZh: 耶和华起了誓，决不后悔，说：你是照著麦基洗德的等次永远为祭司。
prophecies.ntText: And he says in another place, "You are a priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 就如经上又有一处说：「你是照著麦基洗德的等次永远为祭司。」
prophecies.explanation: The Psalms declared a priest unlike any from Aaron's line—one who would serve forever in the order of Melchizedek. Hebrews identifies Jesus as this eternal priest. Unlike the Levitical priests who served temporarily and died, Jesus holds his priesthood permanently, always interceding for his people before God.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言弥赛亚「照麦基洗德的等次永远为祭司」。麦基洗德既是君王又是祭司，预表基督集两者于一身。耶稣同时是大卫宝座的君王和永远代求的祭司。

interpretations.note: Priest forever in Melchizedek order; Payne notes this requires a priest outside the Levitical line
Psalm 110 treated as Messianic throughout; eternal priesthood applied to Messiah in Rabbinic writings

interpretations.title: Priest
interpretations.note: Eternal Melchizedek priesthood; oath of God distinguishes from Aaronic priesthood

prophecies.title: Declared Son of God
prophecies.otText: I will proclaim the LORD's decree: He said to me, "You are my son; today I have become your father."
prophecies.otTextZh: 受膏者说：我要传圣旨。耶和华曾对我说：你是我的儿子，我今日生你。
prophecies.ntText: And a voice from heaven said, "This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 从天上有声音说：「这是我的爱子，我所喜悦的。」
prophecies.explanation: In Psalm 2, God declares 'You are my son' to his anointed king. At Jesus' baptism, the Father's voice from heaven echoed those very words. This was not merely a title of honor but a declaration of divine identity—the eternal Son stepping into his public mission, affirmed by the Father himself.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇记载「你是我的儿子，我今日生你」。耶稣受洗时天父公开宣告「这是我的爱子」。这一预言在拿撒勒人耶稣身上应验，标示弥赛亚正是神的儿子。

interpretations.note: God's king installed on Zion; You are My Son declared at coronation; fulfilled at baptism and resurrection
Explicitly quoted as Messianic in Talmud (Sukk. 52a); applied to the King Messiah in Midrash

interpretations.title: Son of God
interpretations.note: Quoted as Messianic in Talmud (Sukk. 52a); Father's declaration at baptism

prophecies.title: Betrayed by Friend
prophecies.otText: Even my close friend, someone I trusted, one who shared my bread, has turned against me.
prophecies.otTextZh: 连我知己的朋友，我所倚靠、吃过我饭的也用脚踢我。
prophecies.ntText: "I am not referring to all of you; I know those I have chosen. But this is to fulfill this passage of Scripture: 'He who shared my bread has turned against me.'"
prophecies.ntTextZh: 我这话不是指著你们众人说的，我知道我所拣选的是谁。现在要应验经上的话，说：『同我吃饭的人用脚踢我。』
prophecies.explanation: David wrote of a trusted friend who shared his bread turning against him. Jesus quoted this psalm at the Last Supper, knowing Judas would betray him. The pain of betrayal by someone close was not a surprise to God—it was written into the story centuries before, showing that even humanity's worst treachery was part of God's redemptive plan.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言救主「连我知己的朋友」也背叛他。这与犹大出卖耶稣、及彼得三次否认暗合。耶稣在最亲近的关系中仍遭背叛，却仍走向十字架。

interpretations.note: Close friend betrays the psalmist; Payne notes Jesus' explicit citation at Last Supper (John 13:18)
Applied in context of Messiah's betrayal; Psalm 41 cited in Messianic discussions in Talmud

interpretations.title: Betrayed by a Friend
interpretations.note: Familiar friend who ate bread; 'man of my peace' — Judas's kiss of betrayal

prophecies.title: Thirty Pieces of Silver
prophecies.otText: I told them, "If you think it best, give me my pay; but if not, keep it." So they paid me thirty pieces of silver.
prophecies.otTextZh: 我对他们说：「你们若以为美，就给我工价。不然，就罢了！」于是他们给了三十块钱作为我的工价。
prophecies.ntText: and asked, "What are you willing to give me if I deliver him over to you?" So they counted out for him thirty pieces of silver.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 「我把他交给你们，你们愿意给我多少钱？」他们就给了他三十块钱。
prophecies.explanation: Zechariah named the exact price at which the good shepherd would be valued: thirty pieces of silver, the price of a slave. Centuries later, Judas received precisely that amount to betray Jesus. The specificity of this detail—down to the exact sum—reveals how thoroughly God foresaw and wove every detail of the Messiah's story.
prophecies.explanationZh: 撒迦利亚预言弥赛亚被估价三十块银钱，这正是犹大出卖耶稣所得的价钱。马太福音点明这一应验。悖逆的估价被记录，显明受难在上帝计划中并非偶然。

interpretations.note: Thirty pieces of silver; Payne calls this one of the most statistically improbable fulfillments
Messianically explained in Ber. R. 98; thirty pieces of silver applied to Messiah's betrayal

interpretations.title: Sold for Thirty Pieces of Silver
interpretations.note: Seven precise details fulfilled: friend, 30 pieces, silver, thrown, house of Lord, potter

prophecies.title: Money Thrown in Temple
prophecies.otText: And the LORD said to me, "Throw it to the potter"—the handsome price at which they valued me! So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them to the potter at the house of the LORD.
prophecies.otTextZh: 耶和华吩咐我说：「要把众人所估定美好的价值丢给窑户。」我便将这三十块钱，在耶和华的殿中丢给窑户了。
prophecies.ntText: So Judas threw the money into the temple and left. Then he went away and hanged himself.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 犹大就把那银钱丢在殿里，出去吊死了。
prophecies.explanation: Not only was the betrayal price foretold, but Zechariah also described what would happen to the money: it would be thrown to the potter at the house of the Lord. Matthew records that Judas, overcome with remorse, flung the silver coins into the temple. The chief priests then used the money to buy a potter's field—fulfilling every detail of the ancient prophecy.
prophecies.explanationZh: 撒迦利亚预言「丢给窑户」的三十银钱，与犹大把银钱扔进圣殿、祭司用来买窑户之田的记载吻合。马太福音逐项标明这应验。阴谋者的交易成为圣经预言的印证。

interpretations.note: Thirty pieces thrown to potter; same passage as L14, second half of the fulfillment
Continuation of Zech 11 Messianic discourse; potter's field in Rabbinic sources

interpretations.title: Money Thrown into God's House
interpretations.note: Thrown (not placed) into the temple — Matt 27:5 exact fulfillment; also #36 Price Given for Potter's Field

prophecies.title: Hands and Feet Pierced
prophecies.otText: Dogs surround me, a pack of villains encircles me; they pierce my hands and my feet.
prophecies.otTextZh: 犬类围著我，恶党环绕我；他们扎了我的手，我的脚。
prophecies.ntText: So the other disciples told him, "We have seen the Lord!" But he said to them, "Unless I see the nail marks in his hands and put my finger where the nails were, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 那些门徒就对他说：「我们已经看见主了。」多马却说：「我非看见他手上的钉痕，用指头探入那钉痕，又用手探入他的肋旁，我总不信。」
prophecies.explanation: A thousand years before crucifixion was even practiced, the psalmist described having his hands and feet pierced. When Thomas demanded to see the nail marks in Jesus' hands, he was unknowingly confirming the fulfillment of this ancient psalm. The wounds of the cross, far from disproving Jesus' identity, became the very proof that he is the promised Messiah.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言「他们扎了我的手、我的脚」。这描写在罗马钉十字架的残酷刑罚上应验于耶稣。大卫千年前的白描，成为新约记载受难的预表。

interpretations.note: Hands and feet pierced; Payne notes crucifixion unknown in David's era, making this highly specific
Psalm 22 treated as Messianic Passion Psalm; verse cited in Yalkut on Messiah's sufferings

interpretations.title: Hands and Feet Pierced
interpretations.note: Roman crucifixion method; large dull spikes; Zech 12:10 cited as parallel

prophecies.title: Garments Cast Lots
prophecies.otText: They divide my clothes among them and cast lots for my garment.
prophecies.otTextZh: 他们分我的外衣，为我的里衣拈阄。
prophecies.ntText: "Let's not tear it," they said to one another. "Let's decide by lot who will get it." This happened that the scripture might be fulfilled that said, "They divided my clothes among them and cast lots for my garment." So this is what the soldiers did.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他们就彼此说：「我们不要撕开，只要拈阄，看谁得著。」这要应验经上的话说：他们分了我的外衣，为我的里衣拈阄。兵丁果然做了这事。
prophecies.explanation: David described enemies dividing his clothing and gambling for his garment. At the cross, Roman soldiers did exactly that—splitting Jesus' outer garments among themselves and casting lots for his seamless undergarment. John saw this happen and recognized it as Scripture fulfilled, a small, precise detail that no human conspiracy could have staged.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言人分他外衣、为里衣拈阄。兵丁在十字架下正是如此处置耶稣的衣裳。约翰福音特意记下这细节以显明预言被逐个应验。

interpretations.note: Garments divided and lots cast; Payne cites John 19:24 as word-for-word fulfillment
Garments and lots within the Messianic Psalm 22; cited in Rabbinic writings on Messiah's derision

prophecies.title: Mocked While Suffering
prophecies.otText: All who see me mock me; they hurl insults, shaking their heads.
prophecies.otTextZh: 凡看见我的都嗤笑我；他们撇嘴摇头，说：
prophecies.ntText: Those who passed by hurled insults at him, shaking their heads
prophecies.ntTextZh: 从那里经过的人讥诮他，摇著头，说：
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist described being mocked by onlookers who hurl insults and shake their heads. Matthew records this exact scene at Calvary, where passersby taunted Jesus with the very gestures David described. What the world saw as humiliation, Scripture reveals as prophetic fulfillment—every sneer was foreseen, and Jesus endured it willingly.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言救主受难时被摇头讥诮。福音书记载旁观者、祭司与强盗在十字架下讥笑耶稣。连诽谤都在预言中被预告。

interpretations.note: Mockers shake their heads; Payne notes mocking language matches Matthew 27:39–43 precisely
Mocking expressly applied to Messiah's sufferings and derision from enemies in ancient Synagogue commentary

interpretations.title: Mocked
interpretations.note: Shoot out the lip, shake the head — Psalm 22 treated as full Passion Psalm by McDowell

prophecies.title: Given Vinegar
prophecies.otText: They put gall in my food and gave me vinegar for my thirst.
prophecies.otTextZh: 他们拿苦胆给我当食物；我渴了，他们拿醋给我喝。
prophecies.ntText: There they offered Jesus wine to drink, mixed with gall; but after tasting it, he refused to drink it.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 兵丁拿苦胆调和的酒给耶稣喝。他尝了，就不肯喝。
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist cried out about being given gall for food and vinegar for thirst—a picture of cruelty added to suffering. At the cross, soldiers offered Jesus wine mixed with gall, a bitter, numbing drink. Even this seemingly minor act of mockery was foretold centuries earlier, underscoring how completely the details of the crucifixion had been written in advance.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言「我渴了，他们拿醋给我喝」。耶稣在十架上喊「我渴了」，兵丁用海绒蘸醋给他。这一细节同样应验了旧约预言。

interpretations.note: Gall and vinegar offered; Payne cites Matthew 27:34 and John 19:29–30 as dual fulfillments

interpretations.title: To Suffer Thirst
interpretations.note: Vinegar for thirst; John 19:28 — 'I thirst'; also covered by #54 Gall and Vinegar Offered

prophecies.title: Pierced Side
prophecies.otText: And I will pour out on the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and supplication. They will look on me, the one they have pierced, and they will mourn for him as one mourns for an only child, and grieve bitterly for him as one grieves for a firstborn son.
prophecies.otTextZh: 我必将那施恩叫人恳求的灵，浇灌大卫家和耶路撒冷的居民。他们必仰望我（或译：他；本节同），就是他们所扎的；必为我悲哀，如丧独生子，又为我愁苦，如丧长子。
prophecies.ntText: Instead, one of the soldiers pierced Jesus' side with a spear, bringing a sudden flow of blood and water.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 惟有一个兵拿枪扎他的肋旁，随即有血和水流出来。
prophecies.explanation: Zechariah described the people of Jerusalem looking upon the one they had pierced, mourning as for an only son. At the cross, a Roman soldier pierced Jesus' side with a spear. What Zechariah foresaw as a moment of future mourning and repentance began at Calvary—a pierced Messiah whose wounds would become the source of grace for all who look to him in faith.
prophecies.explanationZh: 撒迦利亚预言「他们必仰望我所扎的」。约翰福音记载兵丁扎耶稣的肋旁，有血和水流出。被扎的迹象指向弥赛亚在十架上的真实死亡。

interpretations.note: Look on the one they pierced; Payne notes the first-person divine speaker makes this theologically remarkable

interpretations.title: His Side Pierced
interpretations.note: Laetsch — LORD Jehovah speaks of Himself as pierced; 'thrust through' appears 9x in OT

prophecies.title: Silent Before Accusers
prophecies.otText: He was oppressed and afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; he was led like a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth.
prophecies.otTextZh: 他被欺压，在受苦的时候却不开口（或译：他受欺压，却自卑不开口）；他像羊羔被牵到宰杀之地，又像羊在剪毛的人手下无声，他也是这样不开口。
prophecies.ntText: When he was accused by the chief priests and the elders, he gave no answer.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他被祭司长和长老控告的时候，甚么都不回答。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah pictured the Suffering Servant as silent before his accusers—like a lamb led to slaughter, he would not open his mouth. At his trial, Jesus astonished Pilate by refusing to defend himself. His silence was not weakness but strength under control, fulfilling the prophet's vision of a Servant who willingly submitted to injustice to accomplish God's plan.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言弥赛亚「像羊羔被牵到宰杀之地，在剪毛的人手下无声」。耶稣在大祭司与彼拉多面前几乎一言不答。顺服到极点的静默成为受难的标记。

interpretations.note: Silent before accusers like a lamb; Payne notes the voluntary silence distinguishes this from ordinary suffering
Isaiah 53 treated as most significant Messianic chapter; Messiah's silence before accusers cited in Yalkut

interpretations.title: Silent before Accusers
interpretations.note: Oppressed and afflicted, opened not His mouth; Matt 27:12 fulfillment noted

prophecies.title: Suffering Servant
prophecies.otText: But he was pierced for our transgressions, he was crushed for our iniquities; the punishment that brought us peace was on him, and by his wounds we are healed.
prophecies.otTextZh: 哪知他为我们的过犯受害，为我们的罪孽压伤。因他受的刑罚，我们得平安；因他受的鞭伤，我们得医治。
prophecies.ntText: "He himself bore our sins" in his body on the cross, so that we might die to sins and live for righteousness; "by his wounds you have been healed."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他被挂在木头上，亲身担当了我们的罪，使我们既然在罪上死，就得以在义上活。因他受的鞭伤，你们便得了医治。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah 53 is one of the most striking prophecies of the Messiah's suffering: pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our sins, healed by his wounds. Peter quotes these very words and applies them directly to Christ's death on the cross. The Servant's suffering was not meaningless—it was substitutionary, bearing the penalty that belonged to us so that we could be made whole.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚书五十三章完整描写受苦仆人的画像——他担当我们的罪孽，因他受的鞭伤我们得医治。这章是圣经最集中指向基督受难的预言，新约多处引用在耶稣身上应验。

interpretations.note: Pierced for transgressions; Payne calls Isaiah 53 the most complete messianic prophecy in the OT
Stripes and healing applied to Messiah bearing Israel's sins in Talmud (Sanh. 98b) and Yalkut

interpretations.title: Wounded and Bruised
interpretations.note: Stripes for our healing; Henry cited; Zech 13:6 as parallel

prophecies.title: Buried with Rich
prophecies.otText: He was assigned a grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death, though he had done no violence, nor was any deceit in his mouth.
prophecies.otTextZh: 他虽然未行强暴，口中也没有诡诈，人还使他与恶人同埋；谁知死的时候与财主同葬。
prophecies.ntText: As evening approached, there came a rich man from Arimathea, named Joseph, who had himself become a disciple of Jesus.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 到了晚上，有一个财主，名叫约瑟，是亚利马太来的，他也是耶稣的门徒。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah said the Servant would be assigned a grave with the wicked yet buried with the rich. Jesus was crucified between criminals but laid in the tomb of Joseph of Arimathea, a wealthy man. This unlikely combination—condemned as a criminal, yet honored in burial—fulfilled both halves of Isaiah's prophecy in a single afternoon.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言弥赛亚「与财主同葬」。耶稣死后被亚利马太的约瑟（一位财主）安放在新坟墓里。尊贵却简朴的埋葬正应验这预言。

interpretations.note: Grave with wicked yet rich in death; Payne notes the double prediction (wicked/rich) uniquely fulfilled at Calvary
Burial with the rich in Messianic application of Isa 53 in ancient Rabbinic commentary

interpretations.title: Buried in a Rich Man's Tomb
interpretations.note: Grave with wicked but tomb with rich; Joseph of Arimathea — Stoner probability cited

prophecies.title: Resurrection Foretold
prophecies.otText: because you will not abandon me to the realm of the dead, nor will you let your faithful one see decay.
prophecies.otTextZh: 因为你必不将我的灵魂撇在阴间，也不叫你的圣者见朽坏。
prophecies.ntText: Seeing what was to come, he spoke of the resurrection of the Messiah, that he was not abandoned to the realm of the dead, nor did his body see decay.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 就预先看明这事，讲论基督复活说：他的灵魂不撇在阴间；他的肉身也不见朽坏。
prophecies.explanation: David expressed confidence that God would not let his 'faithful one' see decay. Since David himself died and was buried, Peter argued at Pentecost that David was speaking prophetically about the Messiah. Jesus' resurrection proved that death could not hold him—God's Holy One would never see corruption in the grave.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言「你必不将我的灵魂撇在阴间，也不叫你的圣者见朽坏」。彼得在五旬节指出大卫这话不是指自己，而是预先指向基督的复活。

interpretations.note: Not abandoned to grave nor decay; Payne cites Peter's Pentecost sermon as definitive interpretation
Not suffering corruption applied to Messiah; cited in Rabbinic sources on resurrection hope

interpretations.title: Resurrection
interpretations.note: Soul not left in Sheol; Friedlaender on Ibn Ezra's belief in resurrection; Acts 2:31

prophecies.title: Ascension
prophecies.otText: When you ascended on high, you took many captives; you received gifts from people, even from the rebellious—that you, LORD God, might dwell there.
prophecies.otTextZh: 你已经升上高天，掳掠仇敌；你在人间，就是在悖逆的人间，受了供献，叫耶和华神可以与他们同住。
prophecies.ntText: This is why it says: "When he ascended on high, he took many captives and gave gifts to his people."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 所以经上说：他升上高天的时候，掳掠了仇敌，将各样的恩赐赏给人。
prophecies.explanation: The psalm celebrated God ascending victoriously, receiving gifts from the conquered. Paul applied this to Christ's ascension after the resurrection, reframing the image: Jesus ascended to heaven and poured out spiritual gifts on his church. His victory over sin and death was not just for himself but resulted in gifts—apostles, prophets, teachers—given to build up his people.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言「你已经升上高天」。耶稣复活后四十天在门徒眼前升天，被接到神右边。他的升天开启了坐在宝座上、赐下圣灵的新阶段。

interpretations.note: Ascent on high and captivity applied to Messianic triumph in Talmud and Midrash

interpretations.title: Ascension
interpretations.note: Ascended on high; Acts 1:9 fulfillment; captivity led captive

prophecies.title: Seated at God's Right Hand
prophecies.otText: The LORD says to my lord: "Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet."
prophecies.otTextZh: （大卫的诗。）耶和华对我主说：你坐在我的右边，等我使你仇敌作你的脚凳。
prophecies.ntText: For David did not ascend to heaven, and yet he said, "The Lord said to my Lord: 'Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.'"
prophecies.ntTextZh:
大卫并没有升到天上，但自己说：主对我主说：你坐在我的右边，
等我使你仇敌作你的脚凳。
prophecies.explanation: In Psalm 110, David called someone 'my Lord' and described God inviting that person to sit at his right hand. Peter pointed out that David never ascended to heaven himself—so he must have been speaking of a greater Lord to come. Jesus' ascension and exaltation to God's right hand fulfilled David's prophecy, confirming his authority over all creation.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇「耶和华对我主说：你坐在我的右边」，预告得胜的弥赛亚被高举。新约反复引用此经证明基督复活后的崇高地位，坐在父右边并代求。

interpretations.note: Lord says to my Lord: sit at my right hand; Payne notes Jesus' use of this in Matt 22:44 as self-identification
Ps 110:1 explicitly Messianic; 'Sit at My right hand' applied to Messiah in Talmudic debate (Sanh. 38a)

interpretations.title: He Shall Be Called Lord
interpretations.note: Midrash Tehillim cited; Matt 22:43-45 — David calls Him Lord in the Spirit; also #32 Seated at Right Hand

prophecies.title: Light to the Nations
prophecies.otText: I, the LORD, have called you in righteousness; I will take hold of your hand. I will keep you and will make you to be a covenant for the people and a light for the Gentiles,
prophecies.otTextZh: 我─耶和华凭公义召你，必搀扶你的手，保守你，使你作众民的中保（中保：原文是约），作外邦人的光，
prophecies.ntText: a light for revelation to the Gentiles, and the glory of your people Israel.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 是照亮外邦人的光，又是你民以色列的荣耀。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah described God's Servant as a covenant for the people and a light for the Gentiles. When Simeon held the infant Jesus in the temple, he recognized him as this promised light—a revelation not just for Israel but for all nations. God's salvation was never meant for one people alone; from the beginning, the Messiah was destined to illuminate the whole world.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言弥赛亚要作「外邦人的光」。这打破以色列中心论，表明救恩要临到万民。福音书中耶稣与外邦人的相遇，预示教会将接纳万国。

interpretations.note: Servant as light to nations applied to Messianic era in Targum and Midrash

prophecies.title: Healing Ministry
prophecies.otText: Then will the eyes of the blind be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped. Then will the lame leap like a deer, and the mute tongue shout for joy.
prophecies.otTextZh:
那时，瞎子的眼必睁开；聋子的耳必开通。
那时，瘸子必跳跃像鹿；哑巴的舌头必能歌唱。在旷野必有水发出；在沙漠必有河涌流。
prophecies.ntText: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, those who have leprosy are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is proclaimed to the poor.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 就是瞎子看见，瘸子行走，长大痲疯的洁净，聋子听见，死人复活，穷人有福音传给他们。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah described a future age when the blind would see, the deaf would hear, and the lame would leap for joy. When John the Baptist sent messengers to ask if Jesus was truly the Messiah, Jesus pointed to his miracles—the very signs Isaiah had foretold. His healings were not just acts of compassion; they were credentials proving he was the promised one.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言弥赛亚「担当我们的软弱，背负我们的疾病」。马太福音指出耶稣医治病人正是这预言的应验。身体与灵性的医治在基督服事中合一。

interpretations.note: Opening of blind eyes and ears cited in Messianic context in Yalkut on Isaiah

interpretations.title: Ministry of Miracles
interpretations.note: Blind, deaf, lame, mute healed; Isaiah 32:3-4 also cited; Matt 11:4 fulfillment

prophecies.title: Teaching in Parables
prophecies.otText: I will open my mouth with a parable; I will utter hidden things, things from of old—
prophecies.otTextZh: 我要开口说比喻；我要说出古时的谜语，
prophecies.ntText: Jesus spoke all these things to the crowd in parables; he did not say anything to them without using a parable.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 这都是耶稣用比喻对众人说的话；若不用比喻，就不对他们说甚么。
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist declared he would speak in parables, revealing hidden truths from ancient times. Matthew noted that Jesus taught the crowds entirely in parables, fulfilling this pattern. Jesus' storytelling was not a casual teaching style—it was a prophetic method, concealing deep truths in simple stories so that those with ears to hear could discover the mysteries of God's kingdom.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇与以赛亚都预告弥赛亚用比喻与谜语教导百姓。耶稣大量以比喻讲天国，马太福音点明这是先知预言的应验。比喻既敞开又隐藏天国的奥秘。

interpretations.title: Teacher of Parables
interpretations.note: Parable method predicted; Matt 13:34 — without a parable He did not speak

prophecies.title: Zeal for God's House
prophecies.otText: for zeal for your house consumes me, and the insults of those who insult you fall on me.
prophecies.otTextZh: 因我为你的殿心里焦急，如同火烧，并且辱骂你人的辱骂都落在我身上。
prophecies.ntText: His disciples remembered that it is written: "Zeal for your house will consume me."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他的门徒就想起经上记著说：「我为你的殿心里焦急，如同火烧。」
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist wrote of being consumed by zeal for God's house. When Jesus drove the merchants out of the temple with a whip, overturning tables and scattering coins, his disciples recalled this psalm. Jesus' anger was not reckless—it was righteous passion for his Father's house, which had been turned from a place of prayer into a marketplace.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言「我为你的殿心里焦急，如同火烧」。耶稣洁净圣殿时正是如此。约翰福音引这经文解释他的行动，显明他对圣殿与敬拜的极致看重。

interpretations.title: His Zeal for God
interpretations.note: Fausset cited on John 2:17 as specimen of Messiah's zeal; reproaches falling on Him

prophecies.title: Rejected Stone
prophecies.otText: The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone;
prophecies.otTextZh: 匠人所弃的石头已成了房角的头块石头。
prophecies.ntText: Jesus is "the stone you builders rejected, which has become the cornerstone."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他是你们匠人所弃的石头，已成了房角的头块石头。
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist described a stone that builders threw aside as useless, only for it to become the most important stone in the entire structure. Peter boldly told the religious leaders that Jesus was that rejected stone. The very one the authorities discarded became the cornerstone of God's new building—the church. Rejection by human leaders was part of God's design all along.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言「匠人所弃的石头已成了房角的头块石头」。耶稣引用此经指自己遭犹太领袖弃绝却成为教会的根基。被弃者反成为房角石。

interpretations.note: Rejected stone becomes cornerstone; Payne treats rejection by builders as symbolic of religious establishment's rejection
Rejected stone becoming cornerstone cited as Messianic in Talmud and applied to Messiah in multiple Midrashim

interpretations.title: Rejected Cornerstone
interpretations.note: Stone builders rejected became chief cornerstone; Matt 21:42 fulfillment

prophecies.title: Humble King
prophecies.otText: Rejoice greatly, Daughter Zion! Shout, Daughter Jerusalem! See, your king comes to you, righteous and victorious, lowly and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
prophecies.otTextZh: 锡安的民哪，应当大大喜乐；耶路撒冷的民哪，应当欢呼。看哪，你的王来到你这里！他是公义的，并且施行拯救，谦谦和和地骑著驴，就是骑著驴的驹子。
prophecies.ntText: "Say to Daughter Zion, 'See, your king comes to you, gentle and riding on a donkey, and on a colt, the foal of a donkey.'"
prophecies.ntTextZh: 要对锡安的居民（原文是女子）说：看哪，你的王来到你这里，是温柔的，又骑著驴，就是骑著驴驹子。」
prophecies.explanation: Zechariah described a king who would arrive not on a warhorse but humbly, riding a donkey. On Palm Sunday, Jesus entered Jerusalem on a young donkey, with crowds waving branches and shouting 'Hosanna.' Matthew recognized this as fulfillment of Zechariah's vision: the Messiah's kingdom is built on humility and peace, not military power.
prophecies.explanationZh: 撒迦利亚预言「你的王骑着驴驹而来」,形容弥赛亚是谦和公义的君王。耶稣骑驴进入耶路撒冷正应验此预言。荣入圣城却以谦和的方式宣告王权。

interpretations.note: King comes humble on a donkey; Payne calls the donkey detail a uniquely verifiable fulfillment
Humble King on donkey explicitly applied to Messiah in Talmud (Sanh. 98a) and Midrash with variant readings

interpretations.title: He Was to Enter Jerusalem on a Donkey
interpretations.note: Humble King; Talmud (Sanh. 98a) cited — if Israel worthy, He comes on clouds; if not, on donkey

prophecies.title: Shepherd Struck
prophecies.otText: "Awake, sword, against my shepherd, against the man who is close to me!" declares the LORD Almighty. "Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered, and I will turn my hand against the little ones."
prophecies.otTextZh: 万军之耶和华说：刀剑哪，应当兴起，攻击我的牧人和我的同伴。击打牧人，羊就分散；我必反手加在微小者的身上。
prophecies.ntText: Then Jesus told them, "This very night you will all fall away on account of me, for it is written: 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.'"
prophecies.ntTextZh: 那时，耶稣对他们说：「今夜，你们为我的缘故都要跌倒。因为经上记著说：我要击打牧人，羊就分散了。
prophecies.explanation: Zechariah prophesied that when the shepherd was struck, the sheep would scatter. Jesus quoted this very passage on the night of his arrest, warning the disciples they would all flee. And they did—every one of them. Yet this scattering was not the end of the story; the risen Shepherd would gather his flock again.
prophecies.explanationZh: 撒迦利亚预言「击打牧人，羊就分散」。耶稣在被捕前引用此经，预言门徒将四散。他的被捕击打牧人，羊群暂时分散却终必被再聚。

interpretations.note: Strike the shepherd and sheep scatter; Payne notes Jesus cited this before Gethsemane (Matt 26:31)

interpretations.title: Forsaken by His Disciples
interpretations.note: Laetsch cited on Zech 13:7 as clear prophecy; Christ's own interpretation in Matt 26:31

prophecies.title: Righteous Branch
prophecies.otText: "The days are coming," declares the LORD, "when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, a King who will reign wisely and do what is just and right in the land."
prophecies.otTextZh: 耶和华说：「日子将到，我要给大卫兴起一个公义的苗裔；他必掌王权，行事有智慧，在地上施行公平和公义。
prophecies.ntText: He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David,
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他要为大，称为至高者的儿子；主神要把他祖大卫的位给他。
prophecies.explanation: Jeremiah foretold that God would raise up a righteous Branch from David's line—a king who would reign wisely with justice and righteousness. The angel Gabriel announced to Mary that her son would receive David's throne and be called the Son of the Most High. In Jesus, the long-awaited heir of David's dynasty arrived—not to sit on an earthly throne, but to reign eternally.
prophecies.explanationZh: 耶利米预言大卫要兴起「公义的苗裔」，在地上施行公平。这指向一位兼备公义与救赎的君王。耶稣被称作公义的苗裔，正实现这应许。

interpretations.note: Righteous Branch of David called The LORD Our Righteousness; Payne notes the divine name given to the Branch
Righteous Branch (Tsemach) is one of the best-known Messianic designations; applied in Targum and multiple Midrashim

interpretations.title: House of David
interpretations.note: Righteous Branch; Messiah called Son of David throughout both Talmuds

prophecies.title: Everlasting Kingdom
prophecies.otText: He was given authority, glory and sovereign power; all nations and peoples of every language worshiped him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom is one that will never be destroyed.
prophecies.otTextZh: 得了权柄、荣耀、国度，使各方、各国、各族的人都事奉他。他的权柄是永远的，不能废去；他的国必不败坏。
prophecies.ntText: and he will reign over Jacob's descendants forever; his kingdom will never end.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他要作雅各家的王，直到永远；他的国也没有穷尽。」
prophecies.explanation: Daniel saw a vision of one given everlasting dominion over all nations—a kingdom that would never be destroyed. Gabriel told Mary that her son's kingdom would never end. Every human empire rises and falls, but the kingdom Jesus inaugurated endures forever because its king is eternal. This is the hope at the heart of the gospel: a reign of justice and peace without end.
prophecies.explanationZh: 但以理预言弥赛亚的国度是「永远的国」，永不败坏。天使长加百列向马利亚宣告耶稣的国没有穷尽。基督的国度超越一切世上的帝国。

interpretations.note: Son of Man on clouds given everlasting dominion; Payne sees this as messianic throne-room investiture scene
Son of Man receiving everlasting dominion applied to the Messiah in Talmud and Targum on Daniel

prophecies.title: The Anointed One
prophecies.otText: Know and understand this: From the time the word goes out to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until the Anointed One, the ruler, comes, there will be seven 'sevens,' and sixty-two 'sevens.'
prophecies.otTextZh: 你当知道，当明白，从出令重新建造耶路撒冷，直到有受膏君的时候，必有七个七和六十二个七。正在艰难的时候，耶路撒冷城连街带濠都必重新建造。
prophecies.ntText: The first thing Andrew did was to find his brother Simon and tell him, "We have found the Messiah" (that is, the Christ).
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他先找著自己的哥哥西门，对他说：「我们遇见弥赛亚了。」（弥赛亚翻出来就是基督。）
prophecies.explanation: Daniel received one of the most precise prophecies in Scripture: a timeline pointing to the arrival of the Anointed One. When Andrew found his brother Simon Peter, his words carried centuries of anticipation: 'We have found the Messiah.' The long-awaited Anointed One of Daniel's vision had come, and people recognized it.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇宣告「你已经膏你的神」，但以理称之为「受膏君」。弥赛亚即「受膏者」。耶稣以圣灵受膏完成先知、祭司、君王三重职分。

interpretations.note: Seventy sevens and the Anointed One; Payne provides detailed chronological argument for first-century arrival

prophecies.title: Messiah Cut Off
prophecies.otText: After the sixty-two 'sevens,' the Anointed One will be put to death and will have nothing.
prophecies.otTextZh: 过了六十二个七，那（或译：有）受膏者必被剪除，一无所有；必有一王的民来毁灭这城和圣所，至终必如洪水冲没。必有争战，一直到底，荒凉的事已经定了。
prophecies.ntText: With a loud cry, Jesus breathed his last.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 耶稣大声喊叫，气就断了。
prophecies.explanation: Daniel foretold that the Anointed One would be 'cut off' and have nothing—a shocking statement about the promised Messiah. Mark records the stark fulfillment: with a loud cry, Jesus breathed his last on the cross. The Messiah did not come to seize power but to be cut off for the sake of his people. His death was not a defeat but the culmination of Daniel's prophecy.
prophecies.explanationZh: 但以理预言「受膏者必被剪除，一无所有」。这精确预告弥赛亚的死，并界定了其在历史中的时机。耶稣的十架正是「被剪除」的应验。

interpretations.note: Messiah cut off and has nothing; Payne connects cutting off to Isaiah 53:8 as confirming the death of Messiah

prophecies.title: The Good Shepherd
prophecies.otText: I will place over them one shepherd, my servant David, and he will tend them; he will tend them and be their shepherd.
prophecies.otTextZh: 我必立一牧人照管他们，牧养他们，就是我的仆人大卫。他必牧养他们，作他们的牧人。
prophecies.ntText: "I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 我是好牧人；好牧人为羊舍命。
prophecies.explanation: Ezekiel promised that God would place one shepherd—his servant David—over his people. Jesus declared himself the Good Shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep. Unlike hired hands who flee when danger comes, Jesus willingly gave his life. He is the shepherd Ezekiel foresaw, uniting and caring for God's flock with sacrificial love.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以西结预言上帝要亲自立一位好牧人牧养群羊。耶稣明言「我是好牧人，为羊舍命」。上帝作牧人的应许在基督身上具体成就。

interpretations.note: One shepherd over the flock; Payne sees Ezekiel's shepherd-David as typologically fulfilled by Christ

prophecies.title: Despised and Rejected
prophecies.otText: He was despised and rejected by mankind, a man of suffering, and familiar with pain. Like one from whom people hide their faces he was despised, and we held him in low esteem.
prophecies.otTextZh: 他被藐视，被人厌弃；多受痛苦，常经忧患。他被藐视，好像被人掩面不看的一样；我们也不尊重他。
prophecies.ntText: He came to that which was his own, but his own did not receive him.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他到自己的地方来，自己的人倒不接待他。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah described the Suffering Servant as despised and rejected—a man of sorrows familiar with pain, from whom people turned their faces. John's Gospel echoes this tragedy: Jesus came to his own people, and his own did not receive him. The Creator entered his creation and was turned away. Yet this rejection opened the door for all who would receive him to become children of God.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚描写弥赛亚「被藐视，被人厌弃，多受痛苦」。福音书反复呈现耶稣遭拒、被弃的处境。他的荣耀恰在羞辱中成就。

interpretations.note: Despised and rejected, man of sorrows; Payne notes the social dimension of rejection as distinctive Servant trait
Despised and rejected applied to Messiah's suffering in Yalkut and Talmud (Sanh. 98b)

interpretations.title: Rejected by His Own People
interpretations.note: Henry cited; own brethren disbelieved (John 7:5); own received Him not (John 1:11)

prophecies.title: Crucified with Sinners
prophecies.otText: Therefore I will give him a portion among the great, and he will divide the spoils with the strong, because he poured out his life unto death, and was numbered with the transgressors. For he bore the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.
prophecies.otTextZh: 所以，我要使他与位大的同分，与强盛的均分掳物。因为他将命倾倒，以致于死；他也被列在罪犯之中。他却担当多人的罪，又为罪犯代求。
prophecies.ntText: They crucified two rebels with him, one on his right and one on his left.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他们又把两个强盗和他同钉十字架，一个在右边，一个在左边。（有古卷加：
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah prophesied that the Servant would be numbered with the transgressors—counted among criminals. At the crucifixion, Jesus was placed between two rebels, literally numbered among lawbreakers. He who had no sin was treated as if he were the worst of sinners, fulfilling Isaiah's words and taking on the full weight of human guilt.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言弥赛亚「与罪犯同列」。耶稣被钉在两个罪犯之间，且愿意强盗同在乐园。这应验同钉的预言，也显明赦罪的恩典。

interpretations.note: Numbered with transgressors; Payne connects this to crucifixion between rebels as literal fulfillment
Numbered with transgressors in Messianic application of Isa 53 in Talmud

interpretations.title: Crucified with Thieves
interpretations.note: Numbered with transgressors; crucifixion unknown in Jewish law — Blinzler cited

prophecies.title: Intercedes for Sinners
prophecies.otText: Therefore I will give him a portion among the great, and he will divide the spoils with the strong, because he poured out his life unto death, and was numbered with the transgressors. For he bore the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.
prophecies.otTextZh: 所以，我要使他与位大的同分，与强盛的均分掳物。因为他将命倾倒，以致于死；他也被列在罪犯之中。他却担当多人的罪，又为罪犯代求。
prophecies.ntText: Who then is the one who condemns? No one. Christ Jesus who died—more than that, who was raised to life—is at the right hand of God and is also interceding for us.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 谁能定他们的罪呢？有基督耶稣已经死了，而且从死里复活，现今在神的右边，也替我们祈求（有基督....或译：是已经死了，而且从死里复活，现今在神的右边，也替我们祈求的基督耶稣吗）。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah said the Servant would make intercession for the transgressors. Paul declares in Romans that Christ—having died, risen, and ascended—now sits at God's right hand interceding for us. Jesus' work did not end at the cross or even at the resurrection. Right now he is actively praying for his people, turning Isaiah's ancient promise into a present, living reality.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言弥赛亚「为罪犯代求」。耶稣在十架上说「父啊，赦免他们」，冒着世代的敌意仍代求。他与父之间永远活着也替人代求。

interpretations.note: Made intercession for transgressors; Payne notes the present-tense intercession continues beyond the cross
Intercession for transgressors applied to Messiah's work on behalf of the living and dead in Yalkut

interpretations.title: Made Intercession for Persecutors
interpretations.note: Fausset — began on cross (Luke 23:34), continues in heaven (Heb 9:24; 1 John 2:1)

prophecies.title: Victory Over Death
prophecies.otText: he will swallow up death forever. The Sovereign LORD will wipe away the tears from all faces; he will remove his people's disgrace from all the earth. The LORD has spoken.
prophecies.otTextZh: 他已经吞灭死亡直到永远。主耶和华必擦去各人脸上的眼泪，又除掉普天下他百姓的羞辱，因为这是耶和华说的。
prophecies.ntText: When the perishable has been clothed with the imperishable, and the mortal with immortality, then the saying that is written will come true: "Death has been swallowed up in victory."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 这必朽坏的既变成不朽坏的，这必死的既变成不死的，那时经上所记「死被得胜吞灭」的话就应验了。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah dared to envision a day when God would swallow up death forever. Paul triumphantly declares that this prophecy will be fulfilled when believers receive their resurrection bodies. Death—humanity's oldest enemy—does not get the final word. Through Jesus' resurrection, the ancient promise is set in motion: death itself will be consumed by life.
prophecies.explanationZh: 先知预言死亡被吞灭、坟墓必得胜的哀诉要翻转。基督的复活是对死亡的最终得胜。死亡不再有最后的权势，坟墓也失去它的永远得胜。

interpretations.note: Swallowing up of death applied to Messianic era in Talmud (Moed Katan 28b) and Midrash

prophecies.title: King of Kings
prophecies.otText: Then the sovereignty, power and greatness of all the kingdoms under heaven will be handed over to the holy people of the Most High. His kingdom will be an everlasting kingdom, and all rulers will worship and obey him.
prophecies.otTextZh: 国度、权柄，和天下诸国的大权必赐给至高者的圣民。他的国是永远的；一切掌权的都必事奉他，顺从他。
prophecies.ntText: On his robe and on his thigh he has this name written: KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 在他衣服和大腿上有名写著说：「万王之王，万主之主。」
prophecies.explanation: Daniel saw a vision of God's kingdom receiving absolute sovereignty over all earthly powers. Revelation pulls back the curtain on the future and reveals Jesus bearing the title KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS. Every kingdom, government, and authority will ultimately bow to the one Daniel foresaw. His reign is not a hope deferred—it is an unshakable certainty.
prophecies.explanationZh: 启示录宣告基督被称为「万主之主、万王之王」。这与诗人预言的「万国的王」相呼应。耶稣被高举坐在宝座上，万有都在他权下。

interpretations.note: Kingdom given to the people of the Most High applied to Messianic reign in Talmudic commentary

prophecies.title: Cornerstone
prophecies.otText: So this is what the Sovereign LORD says: "See, I lay a stone in Zion, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone for a sure foundation; the one who relies on it will never be stricken with panic."
prophecies.otTextZh: 所以，主耶和华如此说：看哪，我在锡安放一块石头作为根基，是试验过的石头，是稳固根基，宝贵的房角石；信靠的人必不著急。
prophecies.ntText: For in Scripture it says: "See, I lay a stone in Zion, a chosen and precious cornerstone, and the one who trusts in him will never be put to shame."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 因为经上说：看哪，我把所拣选、所宝贵的房角石安放在锡安；信靠他的人必不至于羞愧。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah described God laying a tested cornerstone in Zion—a sure foundation that would never fail. Peter identifies Jesus as that cornerstone, chosen and precious. In a world of shifting ground, Jesus is the one foundation that holds. Everyone who trusts in him will never be put to shame, no matter what storms come.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言在锡安放一块「宝贵的房角石」。彼得引用此经指向基督。耶稣既是蒙拣选的房角石，也是不信者绊脚的石头。

interpretations.note: Tested cornerstone laid in Zion; Payne links this cornerstone to Ps 118:22 and Isa 8:14 as a stone trilogy
Cornerstone in Zion applied to Messiah by Targum; noted by Rashi; Messiah as crown of glory (Isa 28:5)

prophecies.title: Shepherd King
prophecies.otText: He will stand and shepherd his flock in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God. And they will live securely, for then his greatness will reach to the ends of the earth.
prophecies.otTextZh: 他必起来，倚靠耶和华的大能，并耶和华─他神之名的威严，牧养他的羊群。他们要安然居住；因为他必日见尊大，直到地极。
prophecies.ntText: "I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 我是好牧人；好牧人为羊舍命。
prophecies.explanation: Micah described a ruler from Bethlehem who would shepherd his people in divine strength, bringing security to the ends of the earth. Jesus claimed this identity, declaring himself the Good Shepherd who gives his life for his sheep. His leadership is not domination but sacrificial care—the kind of shepherd-king Micah promised.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以西结和弥迦都预言一位出自大卫、作君王又是牧人的弥赛亚。耶稣同时是牧养群羊的好牧人和统治万有的君王。牧人与君王两种职分在基督身上统一。

prophecies.title: Everlasting Light
prophecies.otText: The sun will no more be your light by day, nor will the brightness of the moon shine on you, for the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory.
prophecies.otTextZh: 日头不再作你白昼的光；月亮也不再发光照耀你。耶和华却要作你永远的光；你神要为你的荣耀。
prophecies.ntText: The city does not need the sun or the moon to shine on it, for the glory of God gives it light, and the Lamb is its lamp.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 那城内又不用日月光照；因有神的荣耀光照，又有羔羊为城的灯。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah envisioned a future when God himself would be his people's everlasting light, replacing the sun and moon. Revelation fulfills this with breathtaking imagery: the heavenly city needs no sun because the glory of God illuminates it, and the Lamb is its lamp. The eternal future is not lit by created lights but by the radiant presence of Christ himself.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言「耶和华要作你永远的光」。新耶路撒冷不需日月光照，因羔羊为城的灯。这指向弥赛亚带来恒久、全然的光。

interpretations.note: Everlasting light replacing sun and moon applied to Messianic era and the light of the Messiah in Yalkut

prophecies.title: Righteous Servant
prophecies.otText: After he has suffered, he will see the light of life and be satisfied; by his knowledge my righteous servant will justify many, and he will bear their iniquities.
prophecies.otTextZh: 他必看见自己劳苦的功效，便心满意足。有许多人因认识我的义仆得称为义；并且他要担当他们的罪孽。
prophecies.ntText: For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 因一人的悖逆，众人成为罪人；照样，因一人的顺从，众人也成为义了。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah said the Righteous Servant would justify many by bearing their iniquities. Paul draws a direct parallel: just as Adam's disobedience made many sinners, Christ's obedience makes many righteous. One man's failure brought ruin; one man's faithfulness brought restoration. Jesus is the obedient Servant whose righteousness counts for all who trust in him.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚书描写「公义的仆人」要使多人归义。耶稣作为神的义仆背负罪孽、称罪人为义。他的顺服使许多人得以称义。

interpretations.note: He will see his offspring and prolong his days; Payne calls the post-death life described here a resurrection prediction
Righteous Servant justifying many cited in Messianic application of Isaiah 53

prophecies.title: Deliverer from Zion
prophecies.otText: "The Redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who repent of their sins," declares the LORD.
prophecies.otTextZh: 必有一位救赎主来到锡安─雅各族中转离过犯的人那里。这是耶和华说的。
prophecies.ntText: and in this way all Israel will be saved. As it is written: "The deliverer will come from Zion; he will turn godlessness away from Jacob."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 于是以色列全家都要得救。如经上所记：必有一位救主从锡安出来，要消除雅各家的一切罪恶；
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah promised a Redeemer coming to Zion for those who repent. Paul quoted this in Romans to affirm that God has not abandoned his ancient people—a deliverer has come from Zion. Jesus' redemptive work reaches beyond any single generation or group; his saving mission extends to all who turn to him.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言「必有一位救主来到锡安」。新约认定耶路撒冷拒绝的救主正是从锡安来的那一位。旧约锡安中心论的应验在基督身上。

interpretations.note: Redeemer coming to Zion applied to Messianic times in Sanh. 98a and Pesiqta 166b

prophecies.title: Child is Born
prophecies.otText: For to us a child is born, to us a son is given, and the government will be on his shoulders. And he will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
prophecies.otTextZh: 因有一婴孩为我们而生；有一子赐给我们。政权必担在他的肩头上；他名称为「奇妙策士、全能的神、永在的父、和平的君」。
prophecies.ntText: Today in the town of David a Savior has been born to you; he is the Messiah, the Lord.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 因今天在大卫的城里，为你们生了救主，就是主基督。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah's grand prophecy of a child born and a son given finds its simplest and most powerful echo in the angel's announcement to the shepherds: a Savior has been born in David's town. The weight of Isaiah's titles—Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God—rested on the shoulders of an infant in a manger. God's greatest gift arrived in the humblest of circumstances.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言「有一婴孩为我们而生」。天使报喜讯向牧羊人宣告救主已在伯利恒降生。以赛亚的尊称——奇妙策士、全能的神——落在马槽里的婴孩身上。上帝最伟大的礼物在最卑微的处境中到来。

interpretations.note: Child born, Son given, Wonderful Counselor; Payne treats the divine names as evidence of Messiah's divine nature
Child born, Son given; names of the Messiah extensively discussed in Talmud (Debarim R.) and Midrash

prophecies.title: Throne Established Forever
prophecies.otText: Of the greatness of his government and peace there will be no end. He will reign on David's throne and over his kingdom, establishing and upholding it with justice and righteousness from that time on and forever. The zeal of the LORD Almighty will accomplish this.
prophecies.otTextZh: 他的政权与平安必加增无穷。他必在大卫的宝座上治理他的国，以公平公义使国坚定稳固，从今直到永远。万军之耶和华的热心必成就这事。
prophecies.ntText: and he will reign over Jacob's descendants forever; his kingdom will never end.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他要作雅各家的王，直到永远；他的国也没有穷尽。」
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah said that the Messiah's government and peace would increase without end, upheld by God's own zeal. Gabriel confirmed to Mary that her son would reign over Jacob's descendants forever. This is not a kingdom sustained by human effort but by the zealous commitment of God Almighty—a throne established by divine power and maintained for eternity.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇与先知书反复宣告大卫的宝座要坚立到永远。天使向马利亚确认耶稣要承受大卫生平宝座、直到永远。弥赛亚的治理不受时间与朝代更迭的限制。

interpretations.note: Government on his shoulders; peace without end; Payne notes the eschatological fullness awaits second advent
Throne established forever applied to Messiah's eternal kingdom in Talmudic and Midrashic sources

prophecies.title: Servant Brings Justice
prophecies.otText: Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen one in whom I delight; I will put my Spirit on him, and he will bring justice to the nations.
prophecies.otTextZh: 看哪，我的仆人─我所扶持所拣选、心里所喜悦的！我已将我的灵赐给他；他必将公理传给外邦。
prophecies.ntText: "Here is my servant whom I have chosen, the one I love, in whom I delight; I will put my Spirit on him, and he will proclaim justice to the nations."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 看哪！我的仆人，我所拣选、所亲爱、心里所喜悦的，我要将我的灵赐给他；他必将公理传给外邦。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah introduced God's chosen Servant, anointed with the Spirit to bring justice to the nations. Matthew recognized this in Jesus—a man empowered by the Spirit at his baptism, who proclaimed God's justice not through military might but through healing, teaching, and sacrificial love. True justice comes not by force but through the Spirit-filled life of the Servant.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言神的仆人要使的审判临到万国、不被折服的公义。耶稣以柔和与信实施行公义，不压伤芦苇。这应许的成就远超政治性的国度想像。

interpretations.note: Servant upheld by God, Spirit upon him; Payne sees the four Servant Songs as a progressive messianic portrait
Servant upheld by God applied to Messiah in Targum and Midrash on Psalm 2

prophecies.title: Gentle Servant
prophecies.otText: He will not shout or cry out, or raise his voice in the streets.
prophecies.otTextZh: 他不喧嚷，不扬声，也不使街上听见他的声音。
prophecies.ntText: "He will not quarrel or cry out; no one will hear his voice in the streets."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他不争竞，不喧嚷；街上也没有人听见他的声音。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah described God's Servant as one who would not shout, quarrel, or raise his voice in the streets. Matthew saw this fulfilled in Jesus' ministry—he did not seek public spectacle or political rallies. His gentleness was not weakness but the quiet strength of one who knew his mission. The Messiah's power was displayed not in loud demands but in compassionate service.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚描写弥赛亚「不喧嚷、不扬声」，柔和不折断压伤的芦苇。马太福音引证耶稣的服事正是如此。他的能力以温柔彰显。

interpretations.note: Will not shout in the streets; Payne contrasts the quiet Servant with false messiahs who sought spectacle
Gentle servant applied to Messiah's ministry manner in Messianic commentary

prophecies.title: Open Blind Eyes
prophecies.otText: to open eyes that are blind, to free captives from prison and to release from the dungeon those who sit in darkness.
prophecies.otTextZh: 开瞎子的眼，领被囚的出牢狱，领坐黑暗的出监牢。
prophecies.ntText: He replied, "Whether he is a sinner or not, I don't know. One thing I do know. I was blind but now I see!"
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他说：「他是个罪人不是，我不知道；有一件事我知道，从前我是眼瞎的，如今能看见了。」
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah prophesied that God's Servant would open the eyes of the blind and free captives from darkness. When Jesus healed the man born blind in John 9, the man's testimony was simple and powerful: 'I was blind but now I see.' Jesus' miracles were not random acts of power—they were signs fulfilling Isaiah's vision of a world set free from darkness.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言弥赛亚「开瞎子的眼，使被掳的得释放」。耶稣医治肉眼与灵眼的瞎盲。马太福音引证这是弥赛亚身份的明证。

interpretations.note: Opening blind eyes applied to Messiah's healing ministry in Yalkut on Isaiah 42

prophecies.title: Good News to the Poor
prophecies.otText: The Spirit of the Sovereign LORD is on me, because the LORD has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim freedom for the captives and release from darkness for the prisoners,
prophecies.otTextZh: 主耶和华的灵在我身上；因为耶和华用膏膏我，叫我传好信息给谦卑的人（或译：传福音给贫穷的人），差遣我医好伤心的人，报告被掳的得释放，被囚的出监牢；
prophecies.ntText: "The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim freedom for the prisoners and recovery of sight for the blind, to set the oppressed free,"
prophecies.ntTextZh: 主的灵在我身上，因为他用膏膏我，叫我传福音给贫穷的人；差遣我报告：被掳的得释放，瞎眼的得看见，叫那受压制的得自由，
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah described the one anointed by God's Spirit to bring good news to the poor, freedom to the captive, and sight to the blind. In the synagogue at Nazareth, Jesus read this passage aloud and then declared, 'Today this scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.' He was not merely reading a text—he was announcing his mission statement.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言受膏者「传好信息给谦卑的人」。耶稣在会堂诵读此经并宣告「今天应验」。福音优先临到贫穷、小民与被压制的群体。

interpretations.note: Spirit anoints to preach good news; Payne notes Jesus stopped reading mid-verse in Nazareth to separate advents
Good news to the poor and liberty to captives applied to Messianic era in Talmud

prophecies.title: Year of the Lord's Favor
prophecies.otText: to proclaim the year of the LORD's favor and the day of vengeance of our God, to comfort all who mourn,
prophecies.otTextZh: 报告耶和华的恩年，和我们神报仇的日子；安慰一切悲哀的人，
prophecies.ntText: "to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 报告神悦纳人的禧年。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah spoke of a coming 'year of the Lord's favor'—a time of divine grace and restoration. When Jesus read this passage in Nazareth, he stopped mid-sentence, omitting the phrase about 'the day of vengeance.' His first coming was about grace, not judgment. The year of favor had arrived in person, and all who would receive it were welcome.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言「耶和华的恩年和报仇之日」。耶稣在拿撒勒会堂引用此经宣告禧年式的好消息。他同时是恩年与审判的应验。

interpretations.note: Year of the LORD's favor; Payne argues the partial reading in Luke 4 is itself prophetically significant
Year of the Lord's favor applied to Messianic proclamation in Rabbinic commentary

prophecies.title: New Covenant
prophecies.otText: "The days are coming," declares the LORD, "when I will make a new covenant with the people of Israel and with the people of Judah."
prophecies.otTextZh: 耶和华说：「日子将到，我要与以色列家和犹大家另立新约，
prophecies.ntText: In the same way, after the supper he took the cup, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 饭后也照样拿起杯来，说：「这杯是用我血所立的新约，是为你们流出来的。
prophecies.explanation: Jeremiah declared that God would one day make a new covenant—not like the one at Sinai that the people broke. At the Last Supper, Jesus took the cup and said, 'This is the new covenant in my blood.' The old covenant was written on stone tablets; the new covenant is sealed with Jesus' own blood and written on human hearts. Jeremiah's hope became reality at a table in Jerusalem.
prophecies.explanationZh: 耶利米预言上帝要与他的百姓另立新约，把律法写在心上。耶稣在最后的晚餐宣告「这杯是用我血所立的新约」。十字架开启新约时代。

interpretations.note: New covenant promise applied to Messianic era; Jer 31:33-34 also cited in Yalkut

prophecies.title: The Lord Our Righteousness
prophecies.otText: In his days Judah will be saved and Israel will live in safety. This is the name by which he will be called: The LORD Our Righteous Savior.
prophecies.otTextZh: 在他的日子，犹大必得救，以色列也安然居住。他的名必称为『耶和华─我们的义』。」
prophecies.ntText: It is because of him that you are in Christ Jesus, who has become for us wisdom from God—that is, our righteousness, holiness and redemption.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 但你们得在基督耶稣里是本乎神，神又使他成为我们的智慧、公义、圣洁、救赎。
prophecies.explanation: Jeremiah gave the coming king a remarkable name: 'The LORD Our Righteousness.' Paul explains that Christ has become our righteousness—not a righteousness we earn but one we receive. We cannot make ourselves right before God, but Jesus can. He is the righteous king Jeremiah promised, and his righteousness becomes ours through faith.
prophecies.explanationZh: 耶利米预言要兴起一位名叫「耶和华我们的义」的君王。耶稣亲自成为信徒的义，满足律法并替我们成就公义。他自己就是那名字的应验。

interpretations.note: The LORD Our Righteousness; Payne sees the divine name as the strongest Davidic messianic title in Jeremiah
'The LORD our Righteousness' cited as one of the Messiah's names in Talmud (Bava Batra 75b)

prophecies.title: Son of Man
prophecies.otText: In my vision at night I looked, and there before me was one like a son of man, coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into his presence.
prophecies.otTextZh: 我在夜间的异象中观看，见有一位像人子的，驾著天云而来，被领到亘古常在者面前，
prophecies.ntText: "You have said so," Jesus replied. "But I say to all of you: From now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Mighty One and coming on the clouds of heaven."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 耶稣对他说：「你说的是。然而，我告诉你们，后来你们要看见人子坐在那权能者的右边，驾著天上的云降临。」
prophecies.explanation: Daniel saw 'one like a son of man' approaching God's throne with the clouds of heaven. At his trial before the high priest, Jesus applied this vision to himself, declaring that they would see the Son of Man seated in power and coming on the clouds. In that moment of apparent defeat, Jesus claimed the highest possible authority—the cosmic sovereignty Daniel had glimpsed in his vision.
prophecies.explanationZh: 但以理书在异象中看见「像人子的」驾云而来得着权柄。耶稣最爱以「人子」自称。这个词既显明他人性，也承载但以理的末世荣耀。

interpretations.note: Son of Man coming on clouds; Payne connects this to the Olivet Discourse and Christ's self-identification throughout the Gospels
Son of Man on clouds applied to Messiah in Talmud (Sanh. 98a) and Targum on Daniel

prophecies.title: Rejected Shepherd
prophecies.otText: Then I took my staff called Favor and broke it, revoking the covenant I had made with all the nations.
prophecies.otTextZh: 我折断那称为「荣美」的杖，表明我废弃与万民所立的约。
prophecies.ntText: He came to that which was his own, but his own did not receive him.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他到自己的地方来，自己的人倒不接待他。
prophecies.explanation: In Zechariah's enacted parable, the shepherd breaks his staff called 'Favor,' symbolizing the end of the covenant relationship. John's Gospel summarizes the tragedy in devastating simplicity: Jesus came to his own people, and they did not receive him. The shepherd was rejected by the very flock he came to save.
prophecies.explanationZh: 撒迦利亚预言牧人被弃绝时羊群遭击打。耶稣被人厌弃却成就救赎。这提醒被弃本身常是进入更伟大应许的路径。

interpretations.note: Breaking of covenant staff in Messianic context of the rejected shepherd

prophecies.title: Darkness at Noon
prophecies.otText: "In that day," declares the Sovereign LORD, "I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight."
prophecies.otTextZh: 主耶和华说：到那日，我必使日头在午间落下，使地在白昼黑暗。
prophecies.ntText: It was now about noon, and darkness came over the whole land until three in the afternoon, for the sun stopped shining.
prophecies.ntTextZh:
那时约有午正，遍地都黑暗了，直到申初，
日头变黑了；殿里的幔子从当中裂为两半。
prophecies.explanation: Amos prophesied that God would make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight. Luke records that during Jesus' crucifixion, darkness covered the land from noon until three in the afternoon. Creation itself responded to the death of its Creator. The supernatural darkness was a sign that something far beyond an ordinary execution was taking place.
prophecies.explanationZh: 阿摩司预言「那日……我必使日头在午间落下，使地在白昼黑暗」。耶稣受难时从午正到申初遍地黑暗。自然界对这黑暗的回应指向审判与受难。

interpretations.title: Darkness over the Land
interpretations.note: Sun darkened at noon; sixth hour = noon, ninth = 3pm by Jewish reckoning; Matt 27:45

prophecies.title: Sun of Righteousness
prophecies.otText: But for you who revere my name, the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its rays. And you will go out and frolic like well-fed calves.
prophecies.otTextZh: 但向你们敬畏我名的人必有公义的日头出现，其光线（原文是翅膀）有医治之能。你们必出来跳跃如圈里的肥犊。
prophecies.ntText: because of the tender mercy of our God, by which the rising sun will come to us from heaven
prophecies.ntTextZh: 因我们神怜悯的心肠，叫清晨的日光从高天临到我们，
prophecies.explanation: Malachi prophesied that the 'sun of righteousness' would rise with healing in its rays for those who revere God's name. Zechariah, the father of John the Baptist, echoed this imagery when he praised God for the 'rising sun' coming from heaven. In Jesus, the long night of waiting ended. The dawn of God's mercy broke over the horizon, bringing healing and hope to a world in darkness.
prophecies.explanationZh: 玛拉基预言「公义的日头」升起，其光线有医治之能。基督的复活如同公义的日头驱散黑暗。这指向末世性的光明与更新。

prophecies.title: Suffering Psalm
prophecies.otText: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from saving me, so far from my cries of anguish?
prophecies.otTextZh: （大卫的诗，交与伶长。调用朝鹿。）我的神，我的神！为甚么离弃我？为甚么远离不救我？不听我唉哼的言语？
prophecies.ntText: About three in the afternoon Jesus cried out in a loud voice, "Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?" (which means "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?").
prophecies.ntTextZh: 约在申初，耶稣大声喊著说：「以利！以利！拉马撒巴各大尼？」就是说：「我的神！我的神！为甚么离弃我？」
prophecies.explanation: The opening cry of Psalm 22—'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?'—became Jesus' own cry from the cross. This was not despair; it was the deliberate identification of Jesus with the suffering described in the psalm. Every detail of Psalm 22 played out at Calvary, from the mocking crowds to the pierced hands. Jesus lived out David's psalm in his own body.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇二十二篇以惊人的精确描写受难细节——手脚被扎、骨头脱臼、分衣拈阄。大卫在苦难中的哀歌成为弥赛亚受难的预表。耶稣在十架上引用这诗篇的第一句。

interpretations.note: My God why have you forsaken me; Payne argues this cry prefigures both the suffering and the ultimate vindication of Ps 22
Opening cry of Psalm 22 applied to Messiah's suffering; entire psalm treated as Messianic in ancient Synagogue

interpretations.title: His Forsaken Cry
interpretations.note: Double cry 'My God' implies clinging to God while forsaken; Matt 27:46 verbatim

prophecies.title: God Will Provide the Lamb
prophecies.otText: Abraham answered, "God himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son." And the two of them went on together.
prophecies.otTextZh: 亚伯拉罕说：「我儿，神必自己预备作燔祭的羊羔。」于是二人同行。
prophecies.ntText: The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, "Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!"
prophecies.ntTextZh: 次日，约翰看见耶稣来到他那里，就说：「看哪，神的羔羊，除去（或译：背负）世人罪孽的！
prophecies.explanation: When Isaac asked his father where the sacrifice was, Abraham answered with prophetic trust: 'God himself will provide the lamb.' Centuries later, John the Baptist pointed to Jesus and declared him the Lamb of God. Abraham's faith-filled words on Mount Moriah found their ultimate answer at the Jordan River—God did provide, and the Lamb he gave takes away the sin of the entire world.
prophecies.explanationZh: 亚伯拉罕在摩利亚山宣告「耶和华必预备」羔羊。约翰称耶稣为「神的羔羊，除去世人罪孽的」。上帝预备的羔羊正是他自己的儿子。

interpretations.note: God will provide the lamb connected to Messianic redemption; Isaac as type of Messiah in Talmud and Midrash

prophecies.title: Star Out of Jacob
prophecies.otText: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob; a scepter will rise out of Israel.
prophecies.otTextZh: 我看他却不在现时；我望他却不在近日。有星要出于雅各，有杖要兴于以色列，必打破摩押的四角，毁坏扰乱之子。
prophecies.ntText: and asked, "Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 「那生下来作犹太人之王的在哪里？我们在东方看见他的星，特来拜他。」
prophecies.explanation: Balaam, a pagan prophet hired to curse Israel, instead foretold a star rising from Jacob—a royal figure who would rule with a scepter. When the Magi followed a star to find the newborn king of the Jews, they were tracing a thread woven into Scripture centuries before. Even the heavens announced what Balaam foresaw: a King had risen in Israel.
prophecies.explanationZh: 巴兰预言「有星要出于雅各，有杖要兴于以色列」。这常被解为弥赛亚的预表。东方的星引导博士寻到婴孩耶稣，印证这古老预言。

interpretations.note: Star from Jacob, scepter from Israel; Payne treats Balaam's oracle as one of the earliest royal messianic predictions
Star out of Jacob applied to the Messiah in Talmud; associated with Bar Kokhba as false messiah (Num. Rab.)

interpretations.title: Son of Jacob
interpretations.note: Star out of Jacob applied to Messiah; eliminates half of Abraham's lineage toward Christ

prophecies.title: Serpent Lifted Up
prophecies.otText: So Moses made a bronze snake and put it up on a pole. Then when anyone was bitten by a snake and looked at the bronze snake, they lived.
prophecies.otTextZh: 摩西便制造一条铜蛇，挂在杆子上；凡被蛇咬的，一望这铜蛇就活了。
prophecies.ntText: Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, that everyone who believes may have eternal life in him.
prophecies.ntTextZh:
摩西在旷野怎样举蛇，人子也必照样被举起来，
叫一切信他的都得永生（或译：叫一切信的人在他里面得永生）。
prophecies.explanation: In the wilderness, those bitten by serpents were healed by looking at a bronze snake lifted on a pole. Jesus used this very image to explain his own crucifixion: just as Moses lifted the serpent, so the Son of Man would be lifted up. The remedy was the same—look and live. Those who look to the crucified Christ in faith receive eternal life.
prophecies.explanationZh: 摩西在旷野举起铜蛇救被蛇咬的百姓。耶稣引用此事自比为「人子必被举起来」。被举起的十字架使凡仰望者得生命。

prophecies.title: Cursed on a Tree
prophecies.otText: you must not leave the body hanging on the pole overnight. Be sure to bury it that same day, because anyone who is hung on a pole is under God's curse.
prophecies.otTextZh: 他的尸首不可留在木头上过夜，必要当日将他葬埋，免得玷污了耶和华─你神所赐你为业之地。因为被挂的人是在神面前受咒诅的。
prophecies.ntText: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us, for it is written: "Cursed is everyone who is hung on a pole."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 基督既为我们受（原文是成）了咒诅，就赎出我们脱离律法的咒诅；因为经上记著：「凡挂在木头上都是被咒诅的。」
prophecies.explanation: The law declared that anyone hung on a tree bore God's curse. Paul's radical claim is that Jesus willingly took on this curse in our place. On the cross, he became the curse so that we could receive the blessing. The very horror of crucifixion—its shame and disgrace—was the means by which God's grace reached humanity.
prophecies.explanationZh: 申命记说「被挂在木头上的人是被咒诅的」。保罗指出基督为我们成为咒诅，为我们挂在木头上。十字架翻转了咒诅成为祝福。

interpretations.note: Curse of one hanged on a tree in Messianic/atonement context in Talmudic sources

prophecies.title: Throne of David Forever
prophecies.otText: Your house and your kingdom will endure forever before me; your throne will be established forever.
prophecies.otTextZh: 你的家和你的国必在我（原文是你）面前永远坚立。你的国位也必坚定，直到永远。』」
prophecies.ntText: He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David, and he will reign over Jacob's descendants forever; his kingdom will never end.
prophecies.ntTextZh:
他要为大，称为至高者的儿子；主神要把他祖大卫的位给他。
他要作雅各家的王，直到永远；他的国也没有穷尽。」
prophecies.explanation: God's promise to David was breathtaking: his throne would last forever. No human dynasty could keep that promise. But when Gabriel told Mary that her son would inherit David's throne and reign without end, the ancient covenant found its fulfillment. Jesus is the eternal King David was promised—the one whose kingdom outlasts every earthly empire.
prophecies.explanationZh: 上帝向大卫应许其后裔宝座存到永远。耶稣被誉为大卫家的后裔，继承这永远的宝座。路加福音详述这是婚约应许的应验。

prophecies.title: Kings Conspire Against the Lord
prophecies.otText: Why do the nations conspire and the peoples plot in vain? The kings of the earth rise up and the rulers band together against the LORD and against his anointed, saying,
prophecies.otTextZh:
外邦为甚么争闹？万民为甚么谋算虚妄的事？
世上的君王一齐起来，臣宰一同商议，要敌挡耶和华并他的受膏者，
prophecies.ntText: You spoke by the Holy Spirit through the mouth of your servant, our father David: "Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain? The kings of the earth rise up and the rulers band together against the Lord and against his anointed one."
prophecies.ntTextZh:
你曾藉著圣灵，托你仆人─我们祖宗大卫的口，说：外邦为甚么争闹？万民为甚么谋算虚妄的事？
