世上的君王一齐起来，臣宰也聚集，要敌挡主，并主的受膏者（或译：基督）。
希律和本丢•彼拉多，外邦人和以色列民，果然在这城里聚集，要攻打你所膏的圣仆（仆：或译子）耶稣，
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist asked why nations rage against God and his anointed. The early church saw this psalm fulfilled when Herod, Pilate, the Gentiles, and Israel's leaders united against Jesus. The conspiracy of the powerful against Christ was not a sign that God's plan had failed—it was the very scenario Scripture had predicted. Their opposition was futile; the anointed King reigns regardless.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇二篇描写列邦君王一同敌挡耶和华并他的受膏者。福音书中所记载的彼拉多与希律、祭司长共谋敌挡基督正是此应验。敌对也成就预言。

interpretations.note: Nations conspiring against God's anointed applied to opposition to the Messiah in Talmud

prophecies.title: Praise from Children
prophecies.otText: Through the praise of children and infants you have established a stronghold against your enemies, to silence the foe and the avenger.
prophecies.otTextZh: 你因敌人的缘故，从婴孩和吃奶的口中，建立了能力，使仇敌和报仇的闭口无言。
prophecies.ntText: "Do you hear what these children are saying?" they asked him. "Yes," replied Jesus, "have you never read, 'From the lips of children and infants you, Lord, have called forth your praise'?"
prophecies.ntTextZh: 对他说：「这些人所说的，你听见了吗？」耶稣说：「是的。经上说『你从婴孩和吃奶的口中完全了赞美』的话，你们没有念过吗？」
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist celebrated how God draws praise from the mouths of children. When children in the temple courts shouted 'Hosanna to the Son of David,' the religious leaders were indignant. Jesus silenced them by quoting this very psalm. God's praise cannot be suppressed—even children declare the truth that the powerful refuse to see.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言「从婴孩和吃奶的口中，你建立了能力」。耶稣荣入圣城时孩童赞美他，引来「你听见了吗」的质疑。平凡人的赞美正是预言所说的能力。

prophecies.title: Into Your Hands
prophecies.otText: Into your hands I commit my spirit; deliver me, LORD, my faithful God.
prophecies.otTextZh: 我将我的灵魂交在你手里；耶和华诚实的神啊，你救赎了我。
prophecies.ntText: Jesus called out with a loud voice, "Father, into your hands I commit my spirit." When he had said this, he breathed his last.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 耶稣大声喊著说：「父啊！我将我的灵魂交在你手里。」说了这话，气就断了。
prophecies.explanation: David prayed 'Into your hands I commit my spirit' as a cry of trust in the midst of suffering. Jesus made these words his final breath on the cross. In his darkest hour, he did not curse or despair—he entrusted himself to his Father. The psalm of trust became the Savior's last prayer, turning death itself into an act of faith.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言「我将我的灵魂交在你手里」。耶稣在十架上最后的话正是引用这祷文。跨出生命的最后一步，他仍有完全的信心。

interpretations.note: Into Your hands cited in Messianic context of suffering and trust in Midrash

interpretations.title: Committed Himself to God
interpretations.note: Into Your hand I commit my spirit; Luke 23:46 — last words on the cross

prophecies.title: False Witnesses Rise Up
prophecies.otText: Ruthless witnesses come forward; they question me on things I know nothing about.
prophecies.otTextZh: 凶恶的见证人起来，盘问我所不知道的事。
prophecies.ntText: Then some stood up and gave this false testimony against him:
prophecies.ntTextZh: 又有几个人站起来作假见证告他，说：
prophecies.explanation: David described ruthless witnesses who accused him of things he knew nothing about. At Jesus' trial before the Sanhedrin, false witnesses stood up with fabricated charges. The injustice of the trial was not an accident—it was the pattern David had experienced and described. Innocent suffering at the hands of liars was written into the Messiah's story from the beginning.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言「说谎的见证人起来作证」。公会的假见证和控告在审判耶稣时出现。正义在假见证面前发声，却不容被辩护。

interpretations.note: False witnesses rising up cited in Messianic commentary on Messiah's trial

interpretations.title: Accused by False Witnesses
interpretations.note: Fierce witnesses rise up; Matt 26:60 — false witnesses sought, found none

prophecies.title: I Come to Do Your Will
prophecies.otText: Sacrifice and offering you did not desire—but my ears you have opened—burnt offerings and sin offerings you did not require. Then I said, "Here I am, I have come—it is written about me in the scroll. I desire to do your will, my God; your law is within my heart."
prophecies.otTextZh:
祭物和礼物，你不喜悦；你已经开通我的耳朵。燔祭和赎罪祭非你所要。
那时我说：看哪，我来了！我的事在经卷上已经记载了。
我的神啊，我乐意照你的旨意行；你的律法在我心里。
prophecies.ntText: Therefore, when Christ came into the world, he said: "Sacrifice and offering you did not desire, but a body you prepared for me; with burnt offerings and sin offerings you were not pleased. Then I said, 'Here I am—it is written about me in the scroll—I have come to do your will, my God.'"
prophecies.ntTextZh:
所以基督到世上来的时候，就说：神啊，祭物和礼物是你不愿意的；你曾给我预备了身体。
燔祭和赎罪祭是你不喜欢的。
那时我说：神啊，我来了，为要照你的旨意行；我的事在经卷上已经记载了。
prophecies.explanation: David declared that God desired not ritual sacrifice but willing obedience: 'Here I am, I have come.' Hebrews applies these words to Christ entering the world—not with an animal offering, but with his own body prepared to do God's will. Jesus replaced an entire sacrificial system with the one offering God truly wanted: a life of perfect obedience.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言弥赛亚「神啊，我来了，为要照你的旨意行」。希伯来书把这话归于基督。他一生献上自己，成就律法与先知的启示。

interpretations.note: Doing God's will cited as Messianic in Talmud; scroll of the book applied to Messiah

prophecies.title: Your Throne, O God
prophecies.otText: Your throne, O God, will last for ever and ever; a scepter of justice will be the scepter of your kingdom. You love righteousness and hate wickedness; therefore God, your God, has set you above your companions by anointing you with the oil of joy.
prophecies.otTextZh:
神啊，你的宝座是永永远远的；你的国权是正直的。
你喜爱公义，恨恶罪恶；所以神─就是你的神─用喜乐油膏你，胜过膏你的同伴。
prophecies.ntText: But about the Son he says, "Your throne, O God, will last for ever and ever; a scepter of justice will be the scepter of your kingdom. You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has set you above your companions by anointing you with the oil of joy."
prophecies.ntTextZh:
论到子却说：神啊，你的宝座是永永远远的；你的国权是正直的。
你喜爱公义，恨恶罪恶；所以神，就是你的神，用喜乐油膏你，胜过膏你的同伴；
prophecies.explanation: In Psalm 45, a royal wedding psalm, the king is addressed as 'God' and given an eternal throne. Hebrews directly applies these words to the Son, declaring that Jesus' throne is God's throne—everlasting and righteous. This is one of the clearest Old Testament affirmations of the Messiah's divine nature, celebrated in the context of a joyful coronation.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇称那受膏者「神啊，你的宝座是永永远远的」。希伯来书直接引用此经论基督的崇高。耶稣永永远远是神，得着永不摇晃的宝座。

interpretations.note: Psalm 45 thoroughly Messianic in Targum; 'Your throne, O God' applied to Messiah's eternal kingship

prophecies.title: Hated Without Reason
prophecies.otText: Those who hate me without reason outnumber the hairs of my head; many are my enemies without cause, those who seek to destroy me. I am forced to restore what I did not steal.
prophecies.otTextZh: 无故恨我的，比我头发还多；无理与我为仇、要把我剪除的，甚为强盛。我没有抢夺的，要叫我偿还。
prophecies.ntText: But this is to fulfill what is written in their Law: 'They hated me without reason.'
prophecies.ntTextZh: 这要应验他们律法上所写的话，说：『他们无故地恨我。』
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist lamented being hated without cause—his enemies outnumbered the hairs on his head. Jesus quoted this very verse, telling his disciples that the world's hatred was not because of anything wrong in him but was the fulfillment of Scripture. Unreasonable hatred of the innocent is not random injustice; it was foretold, and Jesus bore it knowingly.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言「无故恨我的」必多。耶稣说众人都恨他找不到理由。十字架上的恨正是无故的恨，与救主的无罪相对照。

interpretations.title: Hated Without a Cause
interpretations.note: More haters than hairs; John 15:25 — their own law quotes this word as fulfilled

prophecies.title: Kings Bring Gifts
prophecies.otText: May the kings of Tarshish and of distant shores bring tribute to him. May the kings of Sheba and Seba present him gifts. May all kings bow down to him and all nations serve him.
prophecies.otTextZh:
他施和海岛的王要进贡；示巴和西巴的王要献礼物。
诸王都要叩拜他；万国都要事奉他。
prophecies.ntText: On coming to the house, they saw the child with his mother Mary, and they bowed down and worshiped him. Then they opened their treasures and presented him with gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 进了房子，看见小孩子和他母亲马利亚，就俯伏拜那小孩子，揭开宝盒，拿黄金、乳香、没药为礼物献给他。
prophecies.explanation: The psalm envisioned a day when kings from distant lands would bring gifts and bow before Israel's ruler. When the Magi—scholars from the East—arrived with gold, frankincense, and myrrh and fell down to worship the infant Jesus, this royal homage began to be fulfilled. Even as a baby, Jesus drew the reverence of foreign dignitaries.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言列王要献礼物、俯伏臣服于受膏者。博士献上黄金、乳香、没药正是这预言的效验。外邦的代表向这位王致敬。

interpretations.note: Kings bringing gifts applied to the Messiah; entire Psalm 72 viewed as Messianic in Yalkut

interpretations.title: Presented with Gifts
interpretations.note: Kings of Sheba bringing gifts fulfilled by Magi; Isaiah 60:6 cited as parallel

prophecies.title: The Unchanging Creator
prophecies.otText: In the beginning you laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands. They will perish, but you remain; they will all wear out like a garment. Like clothing you will change them and they will be discarded. But you remain the same, and your years will never end.
prophecies.otTextZh:
你起初立了地的根基；天也是你手所造的。
天地都要灭没，你却要长存；天地都要如外衣渐渐旧了。你要将天地如里衣更换，天地就都改变了。
惟有你永不改变；你的年数没有穷尽。
prophecies.ntText: He also says, "In the beginning, Lord, you laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands. They will perish, but you remain; they will all wear out like a garment. You will roll them up like a robe; like a garment they will be changed. But you remain the same, and your years will never end."
prophecies.ntTextZh:
又说：主啊，你起初立了地的根基；天也是你手所造的。
天地都要灭没，你却要长存。天地都要像衣服渐渐旧了；
你要将天地卷起来，像一件外衣，天地就都改变了。惟有你永不改变；你的年数没有穷尽。
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist praised God as the Creator who will outlast his own creation—the heavens will wear out like old clothes, but God remains unchanged. Hebrews applies these very words to the Son, declaring Jesus as the unchanging Creator. Everything else ages, fades, and passes away, but Jesus remains the same yesterday, today, and forever.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言主是起初就有、永不改变的。希伯来书引用此经论到基督的永恒性。耶稣不只是历史中的一个角色，而是创造与更新的主。

interpretations.note: Unchanging Creator applied to Messiah in Talmud; Ps 102:16 applied to Messianic times in Bereshith R.

prophecies.title: Another Takes His Place
prophecies.otText: May his days be few; may another take his place of leadership.
prophecies.otTextZh: 愿他的年日短少！愿别人得他的职分！
prophecies.ntText: "For," said Peter, "it is written in the Book of Psalms: 'May his place be deserted; let there be no one to dwell in it,' and, 'May another take his place of leadership.'"
prophecies.ntTextZh: 因为诗篇上写著，说：愿他的住处变为荒场，无人在内居住；又说：愿别人得他的职分。
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist's curse on a treacherous enemy included the wish that another take his position. Peter applied these words to Judas after his betrayal and death, using them as scriptural warrant for choosing Matthias to replace him among the twelve apostles. Even the vacancy left by the betrayer was covered by Scripture, ensuring the apostolic foundation remained complete.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言「愿别人得他的职分」。使徒行传引此经论到犹大的背叛导致另选使徒接其位。背叛带来的空缺由上帝亲自填补。

prophecies.title: Ever Hearing, Never Understanding
prophecies.otText: He said, "Go and tell this people: 'Be ever hearing, but never understanding; be ever seeing, but never perceiving.' Make the heart of this people calloused; make their ears dull and close their eyes."
prophecies.otTextZh:
他说：「你去告诉这百姓说：你们听是要听见，却不明白；看是要看见，却不晓得。
要使这百姓心蒙脂油，耳朵发沉，眼睛昏迷；恐怕眼睛看见，耳朵听见，心里明白，回转过来，便得医治。」
prophecies.ntText: In them is fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah: "You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving. For this people's heart has become calloused; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes."
prophecies.ntTextZh:
在他们身上，正应了以赛亚的预言，说：你们听是要听见，却不明白；看是要看见，却不晓得；
因为这百姓油蒙了心，耳朵发沉，眼睛闭著，恐怕眼睛看见，耳朵听见，心里明白，回转过来，我就医治他们。
prophecies.explanation: God warned Isaiah that the people would hear his words but not understand, see his works but not perceive. Jesus cited this prophecy to explain why he spoke in parables—many heard his teaching but refused to grasp its meaning. Spiritual blindness is not merely a failure to understand; it is a calloused heart that chooses not to see what is plainly before it.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言百姓对先知的讲论「听是听见却不明白」。耶稣引用此经说明他为何以比喻教导。悖逆的心使预言成为审判而非光照。

interpretations.note: Ever hearing never understanding applied to those rejecting Messiah's message in Midrash

prophecies.title: Branch from Jesse
prophecies.otText: A shoot will come up from the stump of Jesse; from his roots a Branch will bear fruit. The Spirit of the LORD will rest on him—the Spirit of wisdom and of understanding, the Spirit of counsel and of might, the Spirit of the knowledge and fear of the LORD—
prophecies.otTextZh:
从耶西的本（原文是丕）必发一条；从他根生的枝子必结果实。
耶和华的灵必住在他身上，就是使他有智慧和聪明的灵，谋略和能力的灵，知识和敬畏耶和华的灵。
prophecies.ntText: and the Holy Spirit descended on him in bodily form like a dove. And a voice came from heaven: "You are my Son, whom I love; with you I am well pleased."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 圣灵降临在他身上，形状彷佛鸽子；又有声音从天上来，说：「你是我的爱子，我喜悦你。」
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah saw a shoot rising from the stump of Jesse, David's father—an image of new life from what appeared to be a dead dynasty. The Spirit of the Lord would rest on this Branch in fullness. At Jesus' baptism, the Holy Spirit descended visibly, and the Father spoke his approval. The dead stump of David's fallen kingdom had produced its greatest Branch.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言「从耶西的本必发一条」、耶西的根上开枝。罗马书指此预言的应验在「耶西的根」基督身上。被砍下的树根重新发芽承继大卫应许。

interpretations.note: Shoot from Jesse's stump; Payne notes the stump imagery implies a dynasty cut down before the Messiah emerges
Branch from Jesse and Spirit of the LORD extensively applied to Messiah in Targum, Talmud, and Midrash

interpretations.title: Family Line of Jesse
interpretations.note: Targum Isaiah: 'A King shall come forth from the sons of Jesse'; also #20 Special Anointing of Holy Spirit

prophecies.title: Root of Jesse
prophecies.otText: In that day the Root of Jesse will stand as a banner for the peoples; the nations will rally to him, and his resting place will be glorious.
prophecies.otTextZh: 到那日，耶西的根立作万民的大旗；外邦人必寻求他，他安息之所大有荣耀。
prophecies.ntText: And again, Isaiah says, "The Root of Jesse will spring up, one who will arise to rule over the nations; in him the Gentiles will hope."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 又有以赛亚说：将来有耶西的根，就是那兴起来要治理外邦的；外邦人要仰望他。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah described the Root of Jesse as a banner around which the nations would rally. Paul quoted this to emphasize that Jesus' mission extends to all peoples—Gentiles included. The Messiah is not just Israel's king but the hope of the entire world. Every nation finds its rallying point in him, and his resting place—his eternal kingdom—will be glorious.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚与启示录都称弥赛亚为「耶西的根」。耶稣取了大卫的血脉，也超越大卫成为万国的盼望。外邦人与以色列同得这根的恩惠。

interpretations.note: Root of Jesse as banner for peoples; Payne connects this to Gentile inclusion in the messianic community
Root of Jesse as signal to nations applied to Messianic gathering in Talmud and Yalkut

prophecies.title: Voice in the Wilderness
prophecies.otText: A voice of one calling: "In the wilderness prepare the way for the LORD; make straight in the desert a highway for our God."
prophecies.otTextZh: 有人声喊著说：在旷野预备耶和华的路（或译：在旷野，有人声喊著说：当预备耶和华的路），在沙漠地修平我们神的道。
prophecies.ntText: This is he who was spoken of through the prophet Isaiah: "A voice of one calling in the wilderness, 'Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for him.'"
prophecies.ntTextZh: 这人就是先知以赛亚所说的。他说：「在旷野有人声喊著说：预备主的道，修直他的路！」
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah heard a voice calling for a highway to be built in the wilderness for God. Matthew identifies John the Baptist as that voice—preparing the way not through road construction but through calling people to repentance. Before the King arrives, hearts must be made ready. John's wilderness preaching leveled the mountains of pride and filled the valleys of despair.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言「在旷野预备耶和华的路」。施洗约翰正是呼喊的声音，为基督预备道路。旷野成为悔改与遇见神的预备之地。

interpretations.note: Voice in wilderness, prepare the way; Payne calls this the most explicit forerunner prophecy in the OT
Voice in the wilderness preparing the way applied to Messianic forerunner in Rabbinic commentary

interpretations.title: Preceded by Messenger
interpretations.note: John Baptist as forerunner; Mal 3:1 cited in parallel; Luke 1:17 included

prophecies.title: Light for the Gentiles
prophecies.otText: he says: "It is too small a thing for you to be my servant to restore the tribes of Jacob and bring back those of Israel I have kept. I will also make you a light for the Gentiles, that my salvation may reach to the ends of the earth."
prophecies.otTextZh: 现在他说：你作我的仆人，使雅各众支派复兴，使以色列中得保全的归回尚为小事，我还要使你作外邦人的光，叫你施行我的救恩，直到地极。
prophecies.ntText: For this is what the Lord has commanded us: "I have made you a light for the Gentiles, that you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 因为主曾这样吩咐我们说：我已经立你作外邦人的光，叫你施行救恩，直到地极。」
prophecies.explanation: God told his Servant that restoring Israel alone was too small a task—he would be a light for the Gentiles, bringing salvation to earth's ends. Paul and Barnabas quoted this when they turned their mission to the Gentiles. The gospel was never meant for one people only; from the beginning, God's plan was a salvation so vast it encompasses every corner of the globe.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言弥赛亚要作「外邦人的光」，把救恩带到地极。西面在圣殿抱耶稣时称他为「照亮外邦人的光」。这应许在福音传向万民中展开。

interpretations.note: Light to the Gentiles; Payne calls this the clearest statement of universal messianic salvation in the Servant Songs
Light for the Gentiles applied to Messiah's universal mission in Talmud and Midrash

prophecies.title: Back to Those Who Beat Me
prophecies.otText: I offered my back to those who beat me, my cheeks to those who pulled out my beard; I did not hide my face from mocking and spitting.
prophecies.otTextZh: 人打我的背，我任他打；人拔我腮颊的胡须，我由他拔；人辱我，吐我，我并不掩面。
prophecies.ntText: Then they spit in his face and struck him with their fists. Others slapped him
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他们就吐唾沫在他脸上，用拳头打他；也有用手掌打他的，说：
prophecies.explanation: The Servant in Isaiah willingly offered his back to beatings, his cheeks to those who tore out his beard, and his face to mocking and spitting. Matthew records Jesus enduring exactly this treatment—spit on, struck, slapped—after his trial. The Servant did not resist or hide. His willingness to absorb violence without retaliation revealed a strength deeper than any display of power.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚描写弥赛亚「人打我的背，我任他打」。耶稣在受辱中不还口、不还手。他的顺服使全世界的羞辱被吞没。

interpretations.note: Back given to those who beat me; Payne connects to the Sanhedrin trial and Roman scourging as fulfillment
Back given to those who strike applied to Messiah's suffering in Yalkut on Isaiah 50

interpretations.title: Smitten and Spit Upon
interpretations.note: Back to strikers, cheeks to beard-pluckers; Henry commentary; Matt 26:67 fulfillment

prophecies.title: Appearance Disfigured
prophecies.otText: Just as there were many who were appalled at him—his appearance was so disfigured beyond that of any human being and his form marred beyond human likeness—
prophecies.otTextZh: 许多人因他（原文是你）惊奇；他的面貌比别人憔悴；他的形容比世人枯槁。
prophecies.ntText: They put a purple robe on him, then twisted together a crown of thorns and set it on him. And they began to call out to him, "Hail, king of the Jews!" Again and again they struck him on the head with a staff and spit on him.
prophecies.ntTextZh:
他们给他穿上紫袍，又用荆棘编做冠冕给他戴上，
就庆贺他说：「恭喜，犹太人的王啊！」
又拿一根苇子打他的头，吐唾沫在他脸上，屈膝拜他。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah warned that the Servant's appearance would be so disfigured that people would be appalled. Mark's account of Jesus' flogging, the thorns jammed onto his head, and the repeated blows to his face show this prophecy in agonizing detail. The one who was the radiance of God's glory chose to have his human form marred beyond recognition for the sake of those he came to save.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言弥赛亚的面貌「比世人更枯槁、他的形体憔悴」。耶稣受审时的伤损与憔悴应验这预言。他受苦的荣美不同于世界的荣美。

interpretations.note: Servant raised and highly exalted; disfigured appearance; Payne treats 52:13–15 as the heading of the Suffering Servant poem
Disfigured appearance applied to Messiah's suffering; Isa 52-53 treated as continuous Messianic passage

prophecies.title: He Took Our Infirmities
prophecies.otText: Surely he took up our pain and bore our suffering, yet we considered him punished by God, stricken by him, and afflicted.
prophecies.otTextZh: 他诚然担当我们的忧患，背负我们的痛苦；我们却以为他受责罚，被神击打苦待了。
prophecies.ntText: This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah: "He took up our infirmities and bore our diseases."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 这是要应验先知以赛亚的话，说：他代替我们的软弱，担当我们的疾病。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah described the Servant bearing human pain and suffering. Matthew applies this not to the cross but to Jesus' healing ministry—every sick person he healed was a partial fulfillment of this prophecy. Jesus did not merely cure symptoms; he took upon himself the weight of human brokenness. His compassion was not optional; it was his prophetic calling.
prophecies.explanationZh: 马太福音引以赛亚说耶稣「担当我们的软弱，背负我们的疾病」。耶稣的医治与背负，对应以赛亚的应许。身体与灵魂的救恩在十字架上显明。

interpretations.note: He took up our pain and bore our suffering; Payne calls this the substitutionary heart of all OT atonement imagery
Taking our infirmities applied to Messiah bearing Israel's diseases in Talmud (Sanh. 98b)

prophecies.title: Beautiful Feet
prophecies.otText: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news, who proclaim peace, who bring good tidings, who proclaim salvation, who say to Zion, "Your God reigns!"
prophecies.otTextZh: 那报佳音，传平安，报好信，传救恩的，对锡安说：你的神作王了！这人的脚登山何等佳美！
prophecies.ntText: And how can anyone preach unless they are sent? As it is written: "How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!"
prophecies.ntTextZh: 若没有奉差遣，怎能传道呢？如经上所记：「报福音、传喜信的人，他们的脚踪何等佳美！」
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah celebrated the beauty of the messenger who brings good news—peace, salvation, the reign of God. Paul applied this to the gospel messengers who carry the news of Christ to the world. The message itself is glorious, but even the feet that carry it are called beautiful. Every person who shares the good news walks in the footsteps of Isaiah's vision.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚描写「报佳音、传平安之人的脚是何等佳美」。保罗引此指传福音使者。预言指向弥赛亚带来的好消息和传扬这好消息的人。

interpretations.note: Beautiful feet of herald applied to Messianic proclamation; cited in Yalkut with three-day Elijah scenario

prophecies.title: Everlasting Covenant
prophecies.otText: Give ear and come to me; listen, that you may live. I will make an everlasting covenant with you, my faithful love promised to David.
prophecies.otTextZh: 你们当就近我来；侧耳而听，就必得活。我必与你们立永约，就是应许大卫那可靠的恩典。
prophecies.ntText: God raised him from the dead so that he will never be subject to decay. As God has said, 'I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.'
prophecies.ntTextZh: 论到神叫他从死里复活，不再归于朽坏，就这样说：我必将所应许大卫那圣洁、可靠的恩典赐给你们。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah invited the people into an everlasting covenant rooted in God's faithful love promised to David. Paul declared that Jesus' resurrection secured those promises forever—because the risen Christ will never decay, the blessings of David's covenant are now sure and permanent. The resurrection is not just a miracle; it is the guarantee that God's ancient promises will never expire.
prophecies.explanationZh: 历代志与以西结都提说大卫「永远的约」。路加以撒迦利亚的颂歌总结这应许实现在出生之人身上。弥赛亚正是这永约的中心。

interpretations.note: Everlasting covenant and sure mercies of David applied to Messianic era in Talmud

prophecies.title: Rachel Weeping for Her Children
prophecies.otText: This is what the LORD says: "A voice is heard in Ramah, mourning and great weeping, Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted, because they are no more."
prophecies.otTextZh: 耶和华如此说：在拉玛听见号咷痛哭的声音，是拉结哭她儿女，不肯受安慰，因为他们都不在了。
prophecies.ntText: "A voice is heard in Ramah, weeping and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted, because they are no more."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 在拉玛听见号咷大哭的声音，是拉结哭她儿女，不肯受安慰，因为他们都不在了。
prophecies.explanation: Jeremiah described Rachel—the mother of Israel—weeping inconsolably for her lost children. Matthew saw this fulfilled in Herod's massacre of the infants in Bethlehem. The coming of the Messiah did not shield the world from evil; instead, he entered into a world of real suffering. Even the Savior's birth was accompanied by tears, foreshadowing the sorrow he would ultimately bear.
prophecies.explanationZh: 耶利米描写拉结在拉玛为她被掳的儿女哀哭。马太福音引此指伯利恒屠杀无辜婴孩之痛。这悲哀在弥赛亚出生阴影中震动，也预示着更深的悲哀之后是救赎。

interpretations.note: Rachel weeping cited in Messianic context of exile and return in Midrash Rabbah

interpretations.title: Herod Kills Children
interpretations.note: Rachel weeping; Laetsch cited defending Matthew's typological application of Jeremiah 31

prophecies.title: God Sets Up a Kingdom
prophecies.otText: In the time of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will crush all those kingdoms and bring them to an end, but it will itself endure forever.
prophecies.otTextZh: 当那列王在位的时候，天上的神必另立一国，永不败坏，也不归别国的人，却要打碎灭绝那一切国，这国必存到永远。
prophecies.ntText: The seventh angel sounded his trumpet, and there were loud voices in heaven, which said: "The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Messiah, and he will reign for ever and ever."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 第七位天使吹号，天上就有大声音说：世上的国成了我主和主基督的国；他要作王，直到永永远远。
prophecies.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar's dream revealed a succession of earthly empires, all crushed by a kingdom set up by God that would never be destroyed. Revelation shows the final fulfillment: every kingdom of this world becomes Christ's eternal domain. Human empires rise and crumble, but the kingdom God established through Jesus endures forever—unshakeable and unending.
prophecies.explanationZh: 但以理解梦预言神要立一个永不败坏的国。这国度由弥赛亚建立，而非由人手。耶稣所传的天国正是这永恒国度的应验。

interpretations.note: God setting up a kingdom destroying all others applied to Messianic era in Talmud

prophecies.title: Pour Out My Spirit
prophecies.otText: And afterward, I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your old men will dream dreams, your young men will see visions.
prophecies.otTextZh: 以后，我要将我的灵浇灌凡有血气的。你们的儿女要说预言；你们的老年人要做异梦，少年人要见异象。
prophecies.ntText: 'In the last days, God says, I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your young men will see visions, your old men will dream dreams.'
prophecies.ntTextZh: 神说：在末后的日子，我要将我的灵浇灌凡有血气的。你们的儿女要说预言；你们的少年人要见异象；老年人要做异梦。
prophecies.explanation: Joel foresaw a day when God's Spirit would be poured out on all people—sons and daughters, old and young alike. Peter declared this fulfilled at Pentecost when the Spirit fell on the believers and they spoke in tongues. The Spirit that once rested on select prophets and kings now fills every believer, making the entire community of faith a prophetic people.
prophecies.explanationZh: 约珥预言「我要将我的灵浇灌凡有血气的」。彼得在五旬节引此宣告圣灵降临的应验。耶稣升天后赐下圣灵使应许敞开到末世。

prophecies.title: Three Days in the Deep
prophecies.otText: Now the LORD provided a huge fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was inside the fish three days and three nights.
prophecies.otTextZh: 耶和华安排一条大鱼吞了约拿，他在鱼腹中三日三夜。
prophecies.ntText: For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of a huge fish, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 约拿三日三夜在大鱼肚腹中，人子也要这样三日三夜在地里头。
prophecies.explanation: Jonah's three days in the belly of the great fish became, in Jesus' words, a sign pointing directly to his own death and resurrection. Just as Jonah emerged alive after three days in the deep, Jesus would emerge alive from the tomb. What seemed like the end of Jonah's story was actually a rescue—and the same pattern held true at Easter.
prophecies.explanationZh: 约拿在鱼腹中三日三夜，耶稣以此预表自己三日三夜在地里头。出死入生的记号使不信者无辞可答。约拿的故事正是复活的预表。

prophecies.title: Rebuild David's Fallen Tent
prophecies.otText: "In that day I will restore David's fallen shelter—I will repair its broken walls and restore its ruins—and will rebuild it as it used to be, so that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations that bear my name," declares the LORD, who will do these things.
prophecies.otTextZh:
到那日，我必建立大卫倒塌的帐幕，堵住其中的破口，把那破坏的建立起来，重新修造，像古时一样，
使以色列人得以东所余剩的和所有称为我名下的国。此乃行这事的耶和华说的。
prophecies.ntText: 'After this I will return and rebuild David's fallen tent. Its ruins I will rebuild, and I will restore it, that the rest of mankind may seek the Lord, even all the Gentiles who bear my name, says the Lord, who does these things'—
prophecies.ntTextZh:
正如经上所写的：此后，我要回来，重新修造大卫倒塌的帐幕，把那破坏的重新修造建立起来，
叫余剩的人，就是凡称为我名下的外邦人，都寻求主。
prophecies.explanation: Amos prophesied that God would restore David's fallen shelter so that all nations might seek the Lord. James quoted this at the Jerusalem Council to support the inclusion of Gentile believers. The rebuilding of David's tent is not a physical reconstruction—it is the gathering of all peoples into the family of God through Jesus, the son of David.
prophecies.explanationZh: 阿摩司预言要重建大卫倒塌的帐幕。使徒行传引此论到基督建立国际性的教会。大卫家的荣光在弥赛亚身上被重建并扩及万国。

prophecies.title: My Servant, the Branch
prophecies.otText: Listen, High Priest Joshua, you and your associates seated before you, who are men symbolic of things to come: I am going to bring my servant, the Branch.
prophecies.otTextZh: 大祭司约书亚啊，你和坐在你面前的同伴都当听。（他们是作预兆的。）我必使我仆人大卫的苗裔发出。
prophecies.ntText: because of the tender mercy of our God, by which the rising sun will come to us from heaven
prophecies.ntTextZh: 因我们神怜悯的心肠，叫清晨的日光从高天临到我们，
prophecies.explanation: Zechariah announced the coming of God's servant, called 'the Branch'—a title laden with messianic meaning. Zechariah the priest, father of John the Baptist, echoed this when he praised God for the 'rising sun' from heaven. The Branch imagery speaks of new growth from David's line—fresh, living, fruitful. In Jesus, the royal line that seemed cut off sprouted to life again.
prophecies.explanationZh: 耶利米与撒迦利亚称弥赛亚为「我的仆人大卫苗裔」。耶稣作为大卫之苗裔实现先知话。他正是神所立的苗裔支搭帐幕、成为君王与祭司。

prophecies.title: Priest on His Throne
prophecies.otText: Tell him this is what the LORD Almighty says: 'Here is the man whose name is the Branch, and he will branch out from his place and build the temple of the LORD. It is he who will build the temple of the LORD, and he will be clothed with majesty and will sit and rule on his throne. And he will be a priest on his throne. And there will be harmony between the two.'
prophecies.otTextZh:
对他说，万军之耶和华如此说：看哪，那名称为大卫苗裔的，他要在本处长起来，并要建造耶和华的殿。
他要建造耶和华的殿，并担负尊荣，坐在位上掌王权；又必在位上作祭司，使两职之间筹定和平。
prophecies.ntText: Now the main point of what we are saying is this: We do have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven, and who serves in the sanctuary, the true tabernacle set up by the Lord, not by a mere human being.
prophecies.ntTextZh:
我们所讲的事，其中第一要紧的，就是我们有这样的大祭司，已经坐在天上至大者宝座的右边，
在圣所，就是真帐幕里，作执事；这帐幕是主所支的，不是人所支的。
prophecies.explanation: Zechariah described the Branch building the Lord's temple and serving as both king and priest on his throne—roles that were always separate in Israel. Hebrews reveals Jesus as this unique figure: a high priest who sat down on heaven's throne, serving in the true sanctuary. In Christ, the crown and the priestly garments are united in one person, bringing perfect harmony between God's rule and his mercy.
prophecies.explanationZh: 撒迦利亚预言这祭司「坐在宝座上」，指明弥赛亚集祭司与君王于一身。耶稣不是按亚伦的利未职分，而是照麦基洗德的等次永远为祭司。至高的殿中新祭司进入圣所。

interpretations.note: Priest on His throne; Branch building the Temple applied to Messiah in Zechariah Targum

prophecies.title: Elijah Will Come
prophecies.otText: See, I will send the prophet Elijah to you before that great and dreadful day of the LORD comes. He will turn the hearts of the parents to their children, and the hearts of the children to their parents; or else I will come and strike the land with total destruction.
prophecies.otTextZh:
「看哪，耶和华大而可畏之日未到以前，我必差遣先知以利亚到你们那里去。
他必使父亲的心转向儿女，儿女的心转向父亲，免得我来咒诅遍地。」
prophecies.ntText: And if you are willing to accept it, he is the Elijah who was to come.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 你们若肯领受，这人就是那应当来的以利亚。
prophecies.explanation: Malachi closed the Old Testament with a promise that Elijah would return before the great day of the Lord. Jesus declared that John the Baptist was the Elijah who was to come. John did not come with Elijah's fire, but with his Spirit and power—calling families and a nation to repentance, turning hearts back to God, preparing the way for the day of salvation.
prophecies.explanationZh: 玛拉基预言「我必差遣先知以利亚」预备主的日子。耶稣指明施洗约翰就是以利亚预备道路的天职。先知应许的先锋在约翰身上应验。

prophecies.title: Feet on Mount of Olives
prophecies.otText: On that day his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem, and the Mount of Olives will be split in two from east to west, forming a great valley, with half of the mountain moving north and half moving south.
prophecies.otTextZh: 那日，他的脚必站在耶路撒冷前面朝东的橄榄山上。这山必从中间分裂，自东至西成为极大的谷。山的一半向北挪移，一半向南挪移。
prophecies.ntText: "Men of Galilee," they said, "why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen him go into heaven." Then the apostles returned to Jerusalem from the hill called the Mount of Olives.
prophecies.ntTextZh:
「加利利人哪，你们为甚么站著望天呢？这离开你们被接升天的耶稣，你们见他怎样往天上去，他还要怎样来。」
有一座山，名叫橄榄山，离耶路撒冷不远，约有安息日可走的路程。当下，门徒从那里回耶路撒冷去，
prophecies.explanation: Zechariah prophesied that the Lord's feet would stand on the Mount of Olives. It was from the Mount of Olives that Jesus ascended into heaven, and the angels promised he would return the same way. The geography is precise: the exact hill Zechariah named is where Jesus departed and where the promise of his return was given. The story is not over—it awaits its final chapter.
prophecies.explanationZh: 撒迦利亚预言主的日子他的脚站在橄榄山上。耶稣升天正是从橄榄山去，又要照样再来。这座山成为弥赛亚降临在地上的记号。

interpretations.note: Feet on Mount of Olives applied to Messianic advent in Targum on Zechariah 14

prophecies.title: Cut Off from the Living
prophecies.otText: By oppression and judgment he was taken away. Yet who of his generation protested? For he was cut off from the land of the living; for the transgression of my people he was punished.
prophecies.otTextZh: 因受欺压和审判，他被夺去，至于他同世的人，谁想他受鞭打、从活人之地被剪除，是因我百姓的罪过呢？
prophecies.ntText: "In his humiliation he was deprived of justice. Who can speak of his descendants? For his life was taken from the earth."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他卑微的时候，人不按公义审判他（原文是他的审判被夺去）；谁能述说他的世代？因为他的生命从地上夺去。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah described the Servant being taken away by oppression and judgment, cut off from the land of the living. The Ethiopian eunuch was reading this very passage when Philip met him on the desert road. Philip explained that this was about Jesus—unjustly condemned, killed for others' transgressions. The ancient prophecy became the gateway to faith for a man from the ends of the earth.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚五十章与五十三章描写弥赛亚要从活人地被剪除。耶稣在十字架上的死亡正是这预言。被剪除却为人开辟通往神的路。

interpretations.note: Cut off from the living in full Messianic treatment of Isaiah 53

prophecies.title: Sons of the Living God
prophecies.otText: Yet the Israelites will be like the sand on the seashore, which cannot be measured or counted. In the place where it was said to them, 'You are not my people,' there they will be called 'children of the living God.'
prophecies.otTextZh: 然而，以色列的人数必如海沙，不可量，不可数。从前在甚么地方对他们说「你们不是我的子民」，将来在那里必对他们说「你们是永生神的儿子」。
prophecies.ntText: and, "In the very place where it was said to them, 'You are not my people,' there they will be called 'children of the living God.'"
prophecies.ntTextZh: 从前在甚么地方对他们说：你们不是我的子民，将来就在那里称他们为「永生神的儿子」。
prophecies.explanation: Hosea declared that those once called 'not my people' would be called children of the living God. Paul applied this to the inclusion of Gentiles in God's family—those who were once outsiders are now beloved children. The story of Scripture ends where it began: with God's relentless desire to have a people he calls his own, drawn from every nation on earth.
prophecies.explanationZh: 何西阿预言不是神子民的必称为永生神的儿子。保罗引此论到外邦人蒙拣选进入神的家。弥赛亚的救赎使外邦人被收纳为神的儿女。

interpretations.note: Sons of the living God applied to Messianic restoration of Israel in Midrash

prophecies.title: Gentiles Welcomed
prophecies.otText: May God extend Japheth's territory; may Japheth live in the tents of Shem, and may Canaan be the slave of Japheth.
prophecies.otTextZh: 愿神使雅弗扩张，使他住在闪的帐棚里；又愿迦南作他的奴仆。
prophecies.ntText: But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far away have been brought near by the blood of Christ.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 你们从前远离神的人，如今却在基督耶稣里，靠著他的血，已经得亲近了。
prophecies.explanation: Noah's prophecy that Japheth would dwell in Shem's tents foreshadowed Gentiles sharing in Israel's blessings. Paul declares that those once far away have been brought near through Christ's blood.
prophecies.explanationZh: 众先知预言外邦人要来归向神、与以色列一同受祝福。保罗指出凡信基督的无论犹太外邦都在应许上有分。福音拆毁分隔的墙使人同归神。

interpretations.note: Japheth dwelling in Shem tents — Gentile inclusion in Messianic age (Targum Pseudo-Jon.)

prophecies.title: Hidden Manna Revealed
prophecies.otText: He said to Aaron, "Take a jar and put an omer of manna in it. Then place it before the LORD to be kept for the generations to come."
prophecies.otTextZh: 摩西对亚伦说：「你拿一个罐子，盛一满俄梅珥吗哪，存在耶和华面前，要留到世世代代。」
prophecies.ntText: Whoever has ears, let them hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who is victorious, I will give some of the hidden manna.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 圣灵向众教会所说的话，凡有耳的，就应当听！得胜的，我必将那隐藏的吗哪赐给他，并赐他一块白石，石上写著新名；除了那领受的以外，没有人能认识。』」
prophecies.explanation: The manna preserved in the ark pointed to Christ, the true bread from heaven. Jesus promises hidden manna to those who overcome — sustenance the world cannot see or take away.
prophecies.explanationZh: 启示录提到「隐藏的吗哪」作为终极赏赐。耶稣是生命的粮，胜过旷野的吗哪。以色列在旷野吃的吗哪指向将在新耶路撒冷供应的天上的粮。

interpretations.note: Preserved manna to be revealed by Messiah in Mechilta

prophecies.title: Spirit Without Measure
prophecies.otText: I will come down and speak with you there, and I will take some of the power of the Spirit that is on you and put that Spirit on them.
prophecies.otTextZh: 我要在那里降临，与你说话，也要把降于你身上的灵分赐他们，他们就和你同当这管百姓的重任，免得你独自担当。
prophecies.ntText: For the one whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for God gives the Spirit without limit.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 神所差来的就说神的话，因为神赐圣灵给他是没有限量的。
prophecies.explanation: God gave the Spirit to Moses' seventy elders in measured portions — taking from the Spirit on Moses and distributing it among them. But Jesus received the Spirit without any such limit. John declares that God gives the Spirit to His Son without measure, setting Him apart from every prophet and leader who came before.
prophecies.explanationZh: 约翰福音却说父赐圣灵给神的应许者。耶稣受洗时圣灵仿佛鸽子降在他身上。圣灵「无限量」地临到基督，又从他流向教会。

interpretations.note: Spirit of God — His Spirit worth all others combined; Messianic application

prophecies.title: The Firstborn Glory
prophecies.otText: In majesty he is like a firstborn bull; his horns are the horns of a wild ox. With them he will gore the nations, even those at the ends of the earth.
prophecies.otTextZh: 他为牛群中头生的，有威严；他的角是野牛的角，用以抵触万邦，直到地极。这角是以法莲的万万，玛拿西的千千。
prophecies.ntText: Then one of the elders said to me, "Do not weep! See, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has triumphed."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 长老中有一位对我说：「不要哭！看哪，犹大支派中的狮子，大卫的根，他已得胜，能以展开那书卷，揭开那七印。」
prophecies.explanation: Moses blessed Joseph's descendants with imagery of unstoppable strength. Revelation reveals the ultimate firstborn: Christ, the Lion of Judah, who has triumphed over every power.
prophecies.explanationZh: 希伯来书称那救赎者为「长子」，比众弟兄优先。诗篇以长子的头衔描绘弥赛亚。耶稣作为长子，既是继承人又带领许多弟兄进入荣耀。

interpretations.note: Tanchuma applies beauty of firstling bullock to the Messiah

prophecies.title: Son of Pharez
prophecies.otText: This, then, is the family line of Perez: Perez was the father of Hezron.
prophecies.otTextZh: 法勒斯的后代记在下面：法勒斯生希斯仑；
prophecies.ntText: Judah the father of Perez and Zerah, whose mother was Tamar, Perez the father of Hezron.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 犹大从她玛氏生法勒斯和谢拉；法勒斯生希斯仑；希斯仑生亚兰；
prophecies.explanation: Ruth's genealogy traces the line from Perez to David, and Matthew picks up exactly where Ruth left off — all the way to Jesus. The Savior's family tree is full of grace.
prophecies.explanationZh: 创世记记载犹大从法勒斯那家族中得后裔。福音书的族谱确立耶稣从法勒斯一系而出。曲折的谱系仍被神使用，成就弥赛亚家谱。

interpretations.note: Messiah called Son of Pharez — restorer of six lost blessings (Ber. R. 12)

prophecies.title: Horn of Salvation
prophecies.otText: He will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed.
prophecies.otTextZh: 与耶和华争竞的，必被打碎；耶和华必从天上以雷攻击他，必审判地极的人，将力量赐与所立的王，高举受膏者的角。
prophecies.ntText: He has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 在他仆人大卫家中，为我们兴起了拯救的角，
prophecies.explanation: Hannah prophesied about a coming king whose power would be exalted by God. Zechariah declared that God had raised up that horn of salvation in the house of David.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇与撒迦利亚的颂歌称弥赛亚为「拯救的角」。耶稣的能力被形容为一只拯救的角。大卫家的角从卑微的家里竖立起来。

interpretations.note: Horn of anointed exalted — Targum and Midrashim apply to Messiah

prophecies.title: The Humble Exalted
prophecies.otText: You save the humble, but your eyes are on the haughty to bring them low.
prophecies.otTextZh: 困苦的百姓，你必拯救；但你的眼目察看高傲的人，使他降卑。
prophecies.ntText: He has brought down rulers from their thrones but has lifted up the humble.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他叫有权柄的失位，叫卑贱的升高；
prophecies.explanation: David praised God for saving the humble and humbling the proud. Mary echoed the same theme — God brings down the powerful and lifts up the lowly.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇与箴言都预言「凡自卑的必被升高」。耶稣应验此应许，先降卑后升高。教会的道路与弥赛亚一样是降卑后高举。

interpretations.note: Talmud (Sanh. 98a) — humbling the haughty in Messianic days

prophecies.title: David Final Vision
prophecies.otText: These are the last words of David: "The inspired utterance of David son of Jesse, the utterance of the man exalted by the Most High."
prophecies.otTextZh: 以下是大卫末了的话。耶西的儿子大卫得居高位，是雅各神所膏的，作以色列的美歌者，说：
prophecies.ntText: He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他要为大，称为至高者的儿子；主神要把他祖大卫的位给他。
prophecies.explanation: David's last words spoke of being exalted by the Most High. Gabriel told Mary her son would be called the Son of the Most High and receive David's throne.
prophecies.explanationZh: 撒母耳记与诗篇保留了大卫末后关于「公义的掌权者」的遗言。耶稣治国的公义正实现大卫的异象。他不是大卫政治上的继任，而是永恒宝座的承继。

interpretations.note: Targum applies David last words to Messianic prophecy

prophecies.title: The Righteous Ruler
prophecies.otText: He said concerning the God of Israel, the Rock of Israel spoke to me: "He who rules over people must be just, ruling in the fear of God."
prophecies.otTextZh: 以色列的神、以色列的磐石晓谕我说：那以公义治理人民的，敬畏神执掌权柄，
prophecies.ntText: Do not be amazed at this, for a time is coming when all who are in their graves will hear his voice and come out.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 你们不要把这事看作希奇。时候要到，凡在坟墓里的，都要听见他的声音，就出来：
prophecies.explanation: David spoke of a coming righteous ruler appointed by God. Jesus declared He would exercise the ultimate act of righteous rule — calling the dead from their graves.
prophecies.explanationZh: 先知预言一位公义的掌权者要立在地上施行公平。耶稣的国以公义为根基。他判断无私、以牧者的心治理他的百姓。

interpretations.note: Ruling in fear of God — Targum applies to Messiah raising the dead

prophecies.title: Rod of Iron
prophecies.otText: You will break them with a rod of iron; you will dash them to pieces like pottery.
prophecies.otTextZh: 你必用铁杖打破他们；你必将他们如同窑匠的瓦器摔碎。
prophecies.ntText: To the one who is victorious and does my will to the end, I will give authority over the nations — that one will rule them with an iron scepter.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他必用铁杖辖管（辖管：原文是牧）他们，将他们如同窑户的瓦器打得粉碎，像我从我父领受的权柄一样。
prophecies.explanation: Psalm 2 describes the Messiah ruling the nations with an iron rod, shattering all opposition. Jesus promises to share this authority with those who overcome.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言受膏者「必用铁杖打破他们」。启示录形容基督用铁杖辖管列国。这一预言呈现弥赛亚王权的严厉面，正是来信与来审判的双面。

interpretations.note: Nations as iron-shattered inheritance applied to Messiah in Ber. R. 44

prophecies.title: Works Prove His Mission
prophecies.otText: For who is God besides the LORD? And who is the Rock except our God? It is God who arms me with strength and keeps my way secure.
prophecies.otTextZh: 除了耶和华，谁是神呢？除了我们的神，谁是磐石呢？
prophecies.ntText: Do not believe me unless I do the works of my Father. But if I do them, even though you do not believe me, believe the works.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 我若行了，你们纵然不信我，也当信这些事，叫你们又知道又明白父在我里面，我也在父里面。」
prophecies.explanation: David proclaimed that God alone arms His servant with strength and validates His works. Jesus pointed to His own works as proof of His divine mission.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言弥赛亚「使瞎子看见、使瘸腿行走」等奇事。耶稣以此回应施洗约翰的疑问，以他所行的神迹证明身份。身体与灵性的纪法显为弥赛亚的记号。

interpretations.note: Targum applies God works and miracles to the Messiah

prophecies.title: His Anointed
prophecies.otText: He gives his king great victories; he shows unfailing love to his anointed, to David and to his descendants forever.
prophecies.otTextZh: 耶和华赐极大的救恩给他所立的王，施慈爱给他的受膏者，就是给大卫和他的后裔，直到永远。
prophecies.ntText: This is the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah the son of David, the son of Abraham.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 亚伯拉罕的后裔，大卫的子孙（后裔，子孙：原文是儿子；下同），耶稣基督的家谱：
prophecies.explanation: God promised unfailing love to His anointed and David's descendants forever. Matthew opens by identifying Jesus as the Messiah, son of David — the ultimate recipient of that promise.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇记载大卫站在神面前称神为「我的王、我的神」。这句话指向弥赛亚被立为王、受膏为王的身份。耶稣以受膏者的身份进入世界。

interpretations.note: Great deliverance to His king — Jer. Talmud applies to Messiah

prophecies.title: Crowned with Gold
prophecies.otText: You have welcomed him with rich blessings and placed a crown of pure gold on his head.
prophecies.otTextZh: 你以美福迎接他，把精金的冠冕戴在他头上。
prophecies.ntText: On his head are many crowns. He has a name written on him that no one knows but he himself.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他的眼睛如火焰，他头上戴著许多冠冕；又有写著的名字，除了他自己没有人知道。
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist celebrated a king crowned with pure gold. Revelation reveals Christ wearing many crowns — sovereign over every kingdom, authority, and power.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言的受膏者「戴上冠冕」，迎接金冠冕的尊贵。耶稣的异象中戴着许多冠冕。弥赛亚得着的尊荣由许多冠冕显明。

interpretations.note: Crown of pure gold and length of days applied to King Messiah in Midrash

prophecies.title: Fairer Than the Sons of Men
prophecies.otText: You are the most excellent of men and your lips have been anointed with grace, since God has forever blessed you.
prophecies.otTextZh: 你比世人更美；在你嘴里满有恩惠；所以神赐福给你，直到永远。
prophecies.ntText: All spoke well of him and were amazed at the gracious words that came from his lips.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 众人都称赞他，并希奇他口中所出的恩言；又说：「这不是约瑟的儿子吗？」
prophecies.explanation: Psalm 45 praises the king as most excellent, anointed with grace. Hebrews applies this directly to Jesus — the Son whose throne is eternal and whose kingdom is ruled by justice.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇称那受膏者「比世人更美」。耶稣的荣美与尊贵超越人。不是外表的华丽，而是全然圣洁的公义。

interpretations.note: Targum: Thy beauty O King Messiah surpasses that of human children

prophecies.title: Tribes of the Redeemed
prophecies.otText: Gilead is mine, Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is my helmet, Judah is my scepter.
prophecies.otTextZh: 基列是我的，玛拿西也是我的。以法莲是护卫我头的；犹大是我的杖。
prophecies.ntText: Then I heard the number of those who were sealed: 144,000 from all the tribes of Israel.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 我听见以色列人各支派中受印的数目有十四万四千。
prophecies.explanation: God claimed every tribe of Israel as His own. Revelation shows the sealed remnant from all twelve tribes, united under the Lamb.
prophecies.explanationZh: 启示录记载十二支派各有多人蒙救赎。这响应众先知「各国各族被赎民归向神」的应许。神在基督里聚集万国的被赎子民。

interpretations.note: Gilead and Ephraim — Messianic discussion in Bemidbar R. 14

prophecies.title: Days Without End
prophecies.otText: Increase the days of the king's life, his years for many generations.
prophecies.otTextZh: 你要加添王的寿数；他的年岁必存到世世。
prophecies.ntText: The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Messiah, and he will reign for ever and ever.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 第七位天使吹号，天上就有大声音说：世上的国成了我主和主基督的国；他要作王，直到永永远远。
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist prayed for the king's reign to last generations. In Christ, that prayer is answered beyond imagination — He reigns forever and ever.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇描写那王的日子「像月亮这样坚立，直到永远」。弥赛亚的统治没有穷尽。永恒的国度远超出地上王朝的更迭。

interpretations.note: Days added to the King — Targum applies to eternal Messianic reign

prophecies.title: Sun and Moon Endure
prophecies.otText: May he endure as long as the sun, as long as the moon, through all generations.
prophecies.otTextZh: 太阳还存，月亮还在，人要敬畏你，直到万代！
prophecies.ntText: He will reign over Jacob's descendants forever; his kingdom will never end.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他要作雅各家的王，直到永远；他的国也没有穷尽。」
prophecies.explanation: Psalm 72 prays for a king who rules with God's own justice — a reign enduring as long as the sun. Gabriel told Mary her son would reign over Jacob's descendants forever.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言弥赛亚的宝座与日、月同长久。这以受造常存比喻王权的持久。耶稣的统治与神的创造同被视为恒常与可靠。

interpretations.note: Entire Psalm 72 viewed as Messianic in Yalkut and ancient Synagogue commentary

prophecies.title: Sorrow Repaid with Joy
prophecies.otText: Make us glad for as many days as you have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen trouble.
prophecies.otTextZh: 求你照著你使我们受苦的日子，和我们遭难的年岁，叫我们喜乐。
prophecies.ntText: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the old order of things has passed away.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛，因为以前的事都过去了。」
prophecies.explanation: Moses prayed that God would repay suffering with equal joy. Revelation promises the total elimination of sorrow. In Christ, every affliction is answered with eternal gladness.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言「流泪撒种的，必欢呼收割」。耶稣应许哀哭的人将喜乐盈溢。这应许在弥赛亚带来的国度里成就，反转为欢乐。

interpretations.note: Days of affliction repaid in Messianic days — Midrash on Ps 90

prophecies.title: Enemies Made a Footstool
prophecies.otText: The LORD says to my lord: 'Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.'
prophecies.otTextZh: （大卫的诗。）耶和华对我主说：你坐在我的右边，等我使你仇敌作你的脚凳。
prophecies.ntText: Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 所有的天使，神从来对哪一个说：你坐在我的右边，等我使你仇敌作你的脚凳？
prophecies.explanation: David heard God address his Lord: 'Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool.' Hebrews applies this directly to Christ — the risen King enthroned at God's right hand while His enemies are subdued beneath Him.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言耶和华要使他的仇敌作弥赛亚的脚凳。这常被引用证明基督的得胜。具有大能的王权终使其敌人俯伏。

interpretations.note: Verses 8

prophecies.title: Today
prophecies.otText: Today, if only you would hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as you did at Meribah.
prophecies.otTextZh: 因为他是我们的神；我们是他草场的羊，是他手下的民。惟愿你们今天听他的话：
prophecies.ntText: But encourage one another daily, as long as it is called "Today," so that none of you may be hardened by sin's deceitfulness.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 经上说：「你们今日若听他的话，就不可硬著心，像惹他发怒的日子一样。」
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist urged Israel not to harden their hearts when God speaks. Hebrews applies this urgency to every generation — today is always the day to respond to Christ.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇呼唤衪的子民今日听他声音。希伯来书反复引用「今日」，以启示基督成就的时刻。今天的恩典借着弥赛亚随时敞开把人带回神。

interpretations.note: Today if you hear His voice — applied to Messiah coming in Shem. R. 25

prophecies.title: Zion Rebuilt
prophecies.otText: The LORD will rebuild Zion and appear in his glory.
prophecies.otTextZh: 因为耶和华建造了锡安，在他荣耀里显现。
prophecies.ntText: I saw the Holy City, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride beautifully dressed for her husband.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 我又看见圣城新耶路撒冷由神那里从天而降，预备好了，就如新妇妆饰整齐，等候丈夫。
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist foresaw God rebuilding Zion and appearing in glory. Revelation shows the ultimate fulfillment — the new Jerusalem descending from heaven, God's dwelling place with His people forever.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇预言神要再建立锡安，以他的城为荣耀。耶稣的再来与弥赛亚国度使锡安群岭得见。耶路撒冷成为弥赛亚治理的荣耀中心。

interpretations.note: Bereshith R. 56 applies to Messianic times — LORD rebuilds Zion

prophecies.title: He Remembered His People
prophecies.otText: Yet he took note of their distress when he heard their cry; for their sake he remembered his covenant and out of his great love he relented.
prophecies.otTextZh: 然而，他听见他们哀告的时候，就眷顾他们的急难，
prophecies.ntText: He has helped his servant Israel, remembering to be merciful to Abraham and his descendants forever, just as he promised our ancestors.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他扶助了他的仆人以色列，
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist recalled how God remembered His covenant in Israel's darkest hours. Mary's song declares that God has done it again — remembering mercy, helping Israel, fulfilling His ancient promises through Jesus.
prophecies.explanationZh: 撒迦利亚颂歌与诗篇都提到神记念圣约、眷顾他的百姓。天使向牧羊人宣告的这一「救主」正为此而生。以色列的盼望成为众信徒的振奋。

interpretations.note: Long Messianic discussion on God faithfulness in Midrash

prophecies.title: Mouths Filled with Laughter
prophecies.otText: When the LORD restored the fortunes of Zion, we were like those who dreamed. Our mouths were filled with laughter, our tongues with songs of joy.
prophecies.otTextZh: 我们满口喜笑、满舌欢呼的时候，外邦中就有人说：耶和华为他们行了大事！
prophecies.ntText: So with you: Now is your time of grief, but I will see you again and you will rejoice, and no one will take away your joy.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 你们现在也是忧愁，但我要再见你们，你们的心就喜乐了；这喜乐也没有人能夺去。
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist celebrated the overwhelming joy of restoration after exile. Jesus promises His followers the same pattern — present grief will give way to a joy that no one can take away.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇说被掳归回的人满口喜笑。这呼应圣婴带来的大喜信息。在弥赛亚的救赎里，神的百姓从悲哀中转为喜乐地满口歌唱。

interpretations.note: Applied to Messianic joy — laughter among the nations

prophecies.title: Purified for Judgment
prophecies.otText: I will turn my hand against you; I will thoroughly purge away your dross and remove all your impurities.
prophecies.otTextZh: 我必反手加在你身上，炼尽你的渣滓，除净你的杂质。
prophecies.ntText: When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, he will sit on his glorious throne.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 「当人子在他荣耀里、同著众天使降临的时候，要坐在他荣耀的宝座上。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah prophesied God purifying His people by removing all dross. Jesus revealed that He would come in glory to separate and purify — the final judgment that removes every impurity from God's kingdom.
prophecies.explanationZh: 玛拉基预言弥赛亚像炼金之人的火洁净利未人。基督的审判之火为要净化圣洁之民。这预言一方面审判罪恶一方面炼净子民。

interpretations.note: Talmud (Sanh. 98a): Son of David comes after purging of judges

prophecies.title: True Vine, True Branch
prophecies.otText: In that day the Branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the pride and glory of the survivors in Israel.
prophecies.otTextZh: 到那日，耶和华发生的苗必华美尊荣，地的出产必为以色列逃脱的人显为荣华茂盛。
prophecies.ntText: I am the true vine, and my Father is the gardener.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 「我是真葡萄树，我父是栽培的人。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah foresaw a glorious Branch springing from the LORD. Jesus declared Himself the true vine — the living source of fruitfulness. Every branch that remains in Him bears the fruit Isaiah described.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚称以色列为「葡萄树」。耶稣却明言自己是「真葡萄树」，门徒是枝子。弥赛亚正是那真正结出生命果实的葡萄树。

interpretations.note: Targum: Branch of the LORD applied to Messianic times

prophecies.title: The Holy Remnant
prophecies.otText: And though a tenth remains in the land, it will again be laid waste. But as the terebinth and oak leave stumps when they are cut down, so the holy seed will be the stump in the land.
prophecies.otTextZh: 境内剩下的人若还有十分之一，也必被吞灭，像栗树、橡树虽被砍伐，树墩子却仍存留。这圣洁的种类在国中也是如此。
prophecies.ntText: So too, at the present time there is a remnant chosen by grace.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 如今也是这样，照著拣选的恩典，还有所留的余数。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah saw that even after devastating judgment, a holy seed — a stump — would remain. Paul identifies this as the remnant chosen by grace, preserved through Christ. God's people are never fully cut off.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言要留「圣洁的种类」为余民。耶稣来使以色列中的余民得蒙保守。这应许在真正归向弥赛亚的余民身上应验。

interpretations.note: Talmud (Keth. 112b) applies holy seed/stump to Messianic times

prophecies.title: Stone of Stumbling
prophecies.otText: He will be a holy place; for both Israel and Judah he will be a stone that causes people to stumble and a rock that makes them fall.
prophecies.otTextZh: 他必作为圣所，却向以色列两家作绊脚的石头，跌人的磐石；向耶路撒冷的居民作为圈套和网罗。
prophecies.ntText: and, "A stone that causes people to stumble and a rock that makes them fall." They stumble because they disobey the message — which is also what they were destined for.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 又说：作了绊脚的石头，跌人的磐石。他们既不顺从，就在道理上绊跌（或译：他们绊跌都因不顺从道理）；他们这样绊跌也是预定的。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah warned that God Himself would become a stumbling stone. Peter applies this directly to Christ — those who refuse to believe find Him an obstacle, while those who trust find Him the cornerstone.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言弥赛亚「作为绊脚的石头、跌人的磐石」。许多人因拒绝基督而跌倒。同一块石头既成为教会根基也成了不信者的绊脚石。

interpretations.note: Talmud (Sanh. 38a) applies stone of stumbling Messianically

interpretations.title: Stone of Stumbling to Jews
interpretations.note: Targum Isaiah on 8:13-15 cited verbatim; Sanh. 38a Messianic application

prophecies.title: The LORD Reigns
prophecies.otText: The moon will be dismayed, the sun ashamed; for the LORD Almighty will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before its elders — with great glory.
prophecies.otTextZh: 那时，月亮要蒙羞，日头要惭愧；因为万军之耶和华必在锡安山，在耶路撒冷作王；在敬畏他的长老面前，必有荣耀。
prophecies.ntText: Then I heard every creature in heaven and on earth and under the earth and on the sea, and all that is in them, saying: "To him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be praise and honor and glory and power, for ever and ever!"
prophecies.ntTextZh: 我又听见在天上、地上、地底下、沧海里，和天地间一切所有被造之物，都说：但愿颂赞、尊贵、荣耀、权势都归给坐宝座的和羔羊，直到永永远远！
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah foresaw the LORD reigning in glory that outshines the sun and moon. Revelation fulfills this with every creature praising the Lamb on the throne — Christ's glory eclipses all creation.
prophecies.explanationZh: 诗篇多篇宣告「耶和华作王」。新约以耶稣的国度宣告这是应验。弥赛亚亲自显明神作王治理全地。

interpretations.note: Bemidbar R. — LORD of hosts reigns on Mount Zion in Messianic era

prophecies.title: Crown of Glory
prophecies.otText: In that day the LORD Almighty will be a glorious crown, a beautiful wreath for the remnant of his people.
prophecies.otTextZh: 到那日，万军之耶和华必作他余剩之民的荣冠华冕，
prophecies.ntText: And when the Chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the crown of glory that will never fade away.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 到了牧长显现的时候，你们必得那永不衰残的荣耀冠冕。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah promised that God Himself would be a crown of glory to His remnant. Peter connects this to Christ — the Chief Shepherd who bestows an unfading crown of glory on His faithful ones.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言耶和华要「作他百姓的冠冕」。弥赛亚正是这荣耀冠冕的化身。基督既是宝座上被戴冠冕者，也给他的百姓作荣耀的冠冕。

interpretations.note: Targum: Messiah of the LORD of hosts will be a crown of glory

prophecies.title: Spirit on the Waste Places
prophecies.otText: till the Spirit is poured on us from on high, and the desert becomes a fertile field, and the fertile field seems like a forest.
prophecies.otTextZh: 等到圣灵从上浇灌我们，旷野就变为肥田，肥田看如树林。
prophecies.ntText: In the last days, God says, I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your young men will see visions, your old men will dream dreams.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 神说：在末后的日子，我要将我的灵浇灌凡有血气的。你们的儿女要说预言；你们的少年人要见异象；老年人要做异梦。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah foresaw God's Spirit transforming desolation into abundance. At Pentecost, Peter declared this outpouring fulfilled — the Spirit poured on all people, turning spiritual deserts into flourishing life through Christ.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言神「将我的灵浇灌你的后裔」。耶稣升天赐下圣灵浇灌凡有血气的。废坏之地因圣灵更新而复苏。

interpretations.note: Midrash of Lamentations: Spirit poured out in Messianic days

prophecies.title: Comfort Has Come
prophecies.otText: Comfort, comfort my people, says your God. Speak tenderly to Jerusalem, and proclaim to her that her hard service has been completed.
prophecies.otTextZh: 你们的神说：你们要安慰，安慰我的百姓。
prophecies.ntText: Now there was a man in Jerusalem called Simeon, who was righteous and devout. He was waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was on him.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 在耶路撒冷有一个人，名叫西面；这人又公义又虔诚，素常盼望以色列的安慰者来到，又有圣灵在他身上。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah announced that comfort was coming to God's people. Simeon waited his whole life for this consolation — and held it in his arms when he held the infant Jesus. The comfort Isaiah promised has a name.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言「安慰必临到他的百姓」。众先知常以弥赛亚为安慰的应许。西面在圣殿抱婴儿时称那是安慰。基督正是所期盼的安慰的源头。

interpretations.note: Comfort ye — applied to Messianic comfort in Rabbinic sources

prophecies.title: The Acceptable Time
prophecies.otText: This is what the LORD says: "In the time of my favor I will answer you, and in the day of salvation I will help you."
prophecies.otTextZh: 耶和华如此说：在悦纳的时候，我应允了你；在拯救的日子，我济助了你。我要保护你，使你作众民的中保（中保：原文是约）；复兴遍地，使人承受荒凉之地为业。
prophecies.ntText: For he says, "In the time of my favor I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you." I tell you, now is the time of God's favor, now is the day of salvation.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 因为他说：「在悦纳的时候，我应允了你；在拯救的日子，我搭救了你。」看哪，现在正是悦纳的时候！现在正是拯救的日子；
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah prophesied a future day of salvation. Paul declares that day is now — through Christ, the acceptable time has arrived. God's favor is not a distant hope but a present reality for all who believe.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚称「耶和华悦纳之年」为恩典之时。保罗引此指出基督成就救赎的「现在」。今天正是悦纳的时候，借弥赛亚敞开恩门。

interpretations.note: Yalkut: Messiah suffering — in a time of favor I answered you

prophecies.title: Free the Captives
prophecies.otText: to say to the captives, "Come out," and to those in darkness, "Be free!"
prophecies.otTextZh: 对那被捆绑的人说：出来吧！对那在黑暗的人说：显露吧！他们在路上必得饮食，在一切净光的高处必有食物。
prophecies.ntText: He has sent me to proclaim freedom for the prisoners and recovery of sight for the blind, to set the oppressed free.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 主的灵在我身上，因为他用膏膏我，叫我传福音给贫穷的人；差遣我报告：被掳的得释放，瞎眼的得看见，叫那受压制的得自由，
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah foresaw a deliverer who would call captives out of darkness into freedom. Jesus read these words in the Nazareth synagogue and declared them fulfilled in Himself — He is the liberator Isaiah promised.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚预言弥赛亚「使被掳的得释放」。耶稣在会堂引用此经宣告「今天应验」。从罪与死的掳掠中得赦免显为救恩的真实记号。

interpretations.note: Yalkut (vol ii 52b) quotes this as the words of the Messiah to prisoners

prophecies.title: Redeemed Without Money
prophecies.otText: For this is what the LORD says: "You were sold for nothing, and without money you will be redeemed."
prophecies.otTextZh: 耶和华如此说：「你们是无价被卖的，也必无银被赎。
prophecies.ntText: For you know that it was not with perishable things such as silver or gold that you were redeemed from the empty way of life handed down to you from your ancestors, but with the precious blood of Christ.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 知道你们得赎，脱去你们祖宗所传流虚妄的行为，不是凭著能坏的金银等物，
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah declared that God's people would be redeemed without money. Peter reveals the currency of that redemption — not silver or gold but the precious blood of Christ. Our freedom was purchased at infinite cost.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚宣告「你们被掳的不要用银钱救赎」。耶稣以生命为使罪作成的奇妙交换不再需要银钱。弥赛亚以自己为价赎买神百姓。

interpretations.note: Talmud (Sanh. 97b) — redeemed without price applied to Messiah

prophecies.title: Other Sheep I Have
prophecies.otText: Enlarge the place of your tent, stretch your tent curtains wide, do not hold back; lengthen your cords, strengthen your stakes.
prophecies.otTextZh: 要扩张你帐幕之地，张大你居所的幔子，不要限止；要放长你的绳子，坚固你的橛子。
prophecies.ntText: I have other sheep that are not of this sheep pen. I must bring them also. They too will listen to my voice, and there shall be one flock and one shepherd.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 我另外有羊，不是这圈里的；我必须领他们来，他们也要听我的声音，并且要合成一群，归一个牧人了。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah called Israel to expand her tent for the multitudes coming in. Jesus declared He has other sheep beyond Israel's fold — all would become one flock under one shepherd. The tent stretches to cover the world.
prophecies.explanationZh: 耶稣明言「我另外有羊」要带来归于主。这会归于外邦与教会。旧约中神应许万国归向的呼声，在此公开显露出来。

interpretations.note: Vayyikra R. 10 — tent enlarged in Messianic times

prophecies.title: The Bride Husband
prophecies.otText: For your Maker is your husband — the LORD Almighty is his name — the Holy One of Israel is your Redeemer; he is called the God of all the earth.
prophecies.otTextZh: 因为造你的是你的丈夫；万军之耶和华是他的名。救赎你的是以色列的圣者；他必称为全地之神。
prophecies.ntText: One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls full of the seven last plagues came and said to me, "Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 拿著七个金碗、盛满末后七灾的七位天使中，有一位来对我说：「你到这里来，我要将新妇，就是羔羊的妻，指给你看。」
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah identified God as the husband of His people. Revelation reveals the Lamb's bride — the church, united with Christ forever. The marriage metaphor that began in Isaiah finds its ultimate wedding feast in glory.
prophecies.explanationZh: 旧约以婚约比喻神与以色列。耶稣则以自己为新郎。弥赛亚迎娶他的新娘。启示录进入「羔羊婚筵」的高潮。

interpretations.note: Shemoth R. 15 — God as husband expressly applied to Messianic days

prophecies.title: Jeweled Foundations
prophecies.otText: Afflicted city, lashed by storms and not comforted, I will rebuild you with stones of turquoise, your foundations with lapis lazuli.
prophecies.otTextZh: 你这受困苦、被风飘荡不得安慰的人哪，我必以彩色安置你的石头，以蓝宝石立定你的根基；
prophecies.ntText: The foundations of the city walls were decorated with every kind of precious stone.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 城墙的根基是用各样宝石修饰的：第一根基是碧玉；第二是蓝宝石；第三是绿玛瑙；第四是绿宝石；
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah promised that God would rebuild His afflicted city with precious stones. Revelation describes the new Jerusalem with foundations of every precious stone — the afflicted city has become the eternal city of God.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚描写锡安的墙以宝石为基。启示录也以宝石描画新耶路撒冷的根基。这终极的城因弥赛亚而得全然的荣耀。

interpretations.note: Shemoth R. 15 — jeweled foundations in Messianic glory

prophecies.title: I Am the Light
prophecies.otText: Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD rises upon you.
prophecies.otTextZh: 兴起，发光！因为你的光已经来到！耶和华的荣耀发现照耀你。
prophecies.ntText: When Jesus spoke again to the people, he said, "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light of life."
prophecies.ntTextZh: 耶稣又对众人说：「我是世界的光。跟从我的，就不在黑暗里走，必要得著生命的光。」
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah called God's people to rise because their light had come. Jesus declared Himself that light — the glory of the LORD in human form. Those who follow Him walk in the light Isaiah anticipated.
prophecies.explanationZh: 耶稣明言「我是世界的光」。旧约早就预言神的光要照在罪人的黑暗中。弥赛亚正是把神的光带来世上的那一位。

interpretations.note: Targum and Ber. R. — arise shine applied to Messiah bringing light

prophecies.title: Garments of Vengeance
prophecies.otText: He put on righteousness as his breastplate, and the helmet of salvation on his head; he put on the garments of vengeance and wrapped himself in zeal as in a cloak.
prophecies.otTextZh: 他以公义为铠甲（或译：护心镜），以拯救为头盔，以报仇为衣服，以热心为外袍。
prophecies.ntText: He is dressed in a robe dipped in blood, and his name is the Word of God.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他穿著溅了血的衣服；他的名称为神之道。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah described God clothing Himself in righteousness and vengeance. Revelation shows Christ robed in blood-dipped garments — the Word of God who fights for justice and defeats every enemy.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚描写神「以公义为铠甲」。基督作为弥赛亚也要以公义施行报应。这带出末世末日的审判与争战的图像。

interpretations.note: Applied to Messiah coming after destruction of Gentiles in Midrash

prophecies.title: What No Eye Has Seen
prophecies.otText: Since ancient times no one has heard, no ear has perceived, no eye has seen any God besides you, who acts on behalf of those who wait for him.
prophecies.otTextZh: 从古以来，人未曾听见、未曾耳闻、未曾眼见在你以外有甚么神为等候他的人行事。
prophecies.ntText: However, as it is written: "What no eye has seen, what no ear has heard, and what no human mind has conceived" — the things God has prepared for those who love him.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 如经上所记：神为爱他的人所预备的是眼睛未曾看见，耳朵未曾听见，人心也未曾想到的。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah marveled that no eye has seen what God prepares for His people. Paul quotes this to describe the surpassing glory that awaits believers in Christ — beyond imagination, beyond comprehension.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚说「眼睛未曾看见、耳朵未曾听见」，神为爱他的人所预备。保罗以此形容救恩的荣耀。十字架的救赎远超凡人的想象。

interpretations.note: Yalkut on Isa 60 — things prepared for the righteous in Messianic era

prophecies.title: New Heavens New Earth
prophecies.otText: See, I will create new heavens and a new earth. The former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind.
prophecies.otTextZh: 看哪！我造新天新地；从前的事不再被记念，也不再追想。
prophecies.ntText: Then I saw "a new heaven and a new earth," for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and there was no longer any sea.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 我又看见一个新天新地；因为先前的天地已经过去了，海也不再有了。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah prophesied new heavens and a new earth where former sorrows vanish. Revelation shows John seeing this vision fulfilled — the old creation passes away, and everything is made new through Christ.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以赛亚应许「新天新地」的来临。启示录末后描写的新天新地与这预言呼应。弥赛亚国度的完全成就超越所有黑暗与死亡。

interpretations.note: Midrash on Lamentations — new heavens and earth in Messianic times

prophecies.title: Born Before the Pain
prophecies.otText: Before she goes into labor, she gives birth; before the pains come upon her, she delivers a son.
prophecies.otTextZh: 锡安未曾劬劳就生产，未觉疼痛就生出男孩。
prophecies.ntText: She gave birth to a son, a male child, who will rule all the nations with an iron scepter. And her child was snatched up to God and to his throne.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 妇人生了一个男孩子，是将来要用铁杖辖管（辖管：原文是牧）万国的；她的孩子被提到神宝座那里去了。
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah prophesied a miraculous birth — a son delivered before labor pains. Revelation identifies this child as the one who rules all nations, snatched to God's throne. The Messiah's birth defied natural order.
prophecies.explanationZh: 弥迦预言在苦难之前将生出一位掌权者。耶稣在苦难中降生却开启蒙拯救的新章节。这预言着重以救赎打破咒诅的时刻。

interpretations.note: Vayyikra R. 14 — child born before Zion travails; Messiah before oppressor

prophecies.title: The Throne in Jerusalem
prophecies.otText: At that time they will call Jerusalem The Throne of the LORD, and all nations will gather in Jerusalem to honor the name of the LORD.
prophecies.otTextZh: 那时，人必称耶路撒冷为耶和华的宝座；万国必到耶路撒冷，在耶和华立名的地方聚集。他们必不再随从自己顽梗的恶心行事。
prophecies.ntText: The throne of God and of the Lamb will be in the city, and his servants will serve him.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 以后再没有咒诅；在城里有神和羔羊的宝座；他的仆人都要事奉他，
prophecies.explanation: Jeremiah foresaw Jerusalem becoming the throne of the LORD where all nations gather. Revelation fulfills this — God and the Lamb share the throne in the eternal city, and His servants worship Him forever.
prophecies.explanationZh: 耶利米预言他的宝座设在耶路撒冷。弥赛亚的治理以圣城为中心。这回应大卫家统治的应许在基督身上重生。

interpretations.note: Yalkut on Josh 3:9 — Jerusalem throne of God in Messianic days

prophecies.title: He Who Draws Near
prophecies.otText: Their leader will be one of their own; their ruler will arise from among them. I will bring him near and he will come close to me — for who is he who will devote himself to be close to me?
prophecies.otTextZh: 他们的君王必是属乎他们的；掌权的必从他们中间而出。我要使他就近我，他也要亲近我；不然，谁有胆量亲近我呢？这是耶和华说的。
prophecies.ntText: Therefore he is able to save completely those who come to God through him, because he always lives to intercede for them.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 凡靠著他进到神面前的人，他都能拯救到底；因为他是长远活著，替他们祈求。
prophecies.explanation: Jeremiah foresaw a ruler arising from His own people who draws near to God. Hebrews reveals Christ as this mediator — one of us yet close to God, always living to intercede for those who come through Him.
prophecies.explanationZh: 希伯来书呼唤「进前来的人」得完全。圣约百姓借弥赛亚得以亲近神。耶利米预言的新约应许成就在靠近这位神的人身上。

interpretations.note: Targum applies — Messiah as noble ruler who approaches God

prophecies.title: Law on Our Hearts
prophecies.otText: I will put my law in their minds and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
prophecies.otTextZh: 耶和华说：「那些日子以后，我与以色列家所立的约乃是这样：我要将我的律法放在他们里面，写在他们心上。我要作他们的神，他们要作我的子民。
prophecies.ntText: This is the covenant I will establish with the people of Israel after that time, declares the Lord. I will put my laws in their minds and write them on their hearts.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 主又说：那些日子以后，我与以色列家所立的约乃是这样：我要将我的律法放在他们里面，写在他们心上；我要作他们的神；他们要作我的子民。
prophecies.explanation: Jeremiah prophesied a new covenant with God's law written on hearts, not stone. Hebrews declares this fulfilled in Christ — the new covenant transforms believers from the inside out.
prophecies.explanationZh: 耶利米预言新约「写在他们心上」。圣灵将律法内化于信徒，不再只是外在字句。弥赛亚所立的新约真正改变人心。

interpretations.note: Law written on hearts — applied to Messianic covenant in Yalkut

prophecies.title: He Calls His Own
prophecies.otText: He will give a shout, like those who tread the grapes, against all who live on the earth. He will count them as his flock.
prophecies.otTextZh: 在山地的城邑、高原的城邑、南地的城邑、便雅悯地、耶路撒冷四围的各处，和犹大的城邑必再有羊群从数点的人手下经过。这是耶和华说的。」
prophecies.ntText: He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 看门的就给他开门；羊也听他的声音。他按著名叫自己的羊，把羊领出来。
prophecies.explanation: Jeremiah spoke of God gathering His flock with authority. Jesus identifies Himself as the good shepherd who calls His own sheep by name. The cosmic shepherd knows each one personally.
prophecies.explanationZh: 好牧人耶稣认识他的羊且羊认识他。诗篇与先知都形容牧人亲密引领群羊。弥赛亚作牧人把与神相爱相知的关系赐下。

interpretations.note: Targum: people shall pass under the hands of the Messiah to be numbered

prophecies.title: Times of Restoration
prophecies.otText: When I bring back their captives — the captives of Sodom and her daughters, and the captives of Samaria and her daughters — then I will also bring back your captives along with them.
prophecies.otTextZh: 你的妹妹所多玛和她的众女必归回原位；撒马利亚和她的众女，你和你的众女，也必归回原位。
prophecies.ntText: Heaven must receive him until the time comes for God to restore everything, as he promised long ago through his holy prophets.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 天必留他，等到万物复兴的时候，就是神从创世以来、藉著圣先知的口所说的。
prophecies.explanation: Ezekiel foresaw a time of total restoration — even for the most unexpected peoples. Peter declared that Christ remains in heaven until the time of universal restoration that the prophets promised.
prophecies.explanationZh: 使徒行传引应许「万物复兴的时候」的来临。彼得指预言的复兴发生于主再来。新约关于复活的应许正是此预言的展开。

interpretations.note: Ten things renewed in Messianic days including rebuilding ruins (Midrash)

prophecies.title: Judgment of the Nations
prophecies.otText: I will carry out great vengeance on them and punish them in my wrath. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I take vengeance on them.
prophecies.otTextZh: 我必藉我民以色列的手报复以东；以色列民必照我的怒气，按我的忿怒在以东施报，以东人就知道是我施报。这是主耶和华说的。」
prophecies.ntText: The armies of heaven were following him, riding on white horses and dressed in fine linen, white and clean.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 在天上的众军骑著白马，穿著细麻衣，又白又洁，跟随他。
prophecies.explanation: Ezekiel foretold God's vengeance on the nations that opposed His people. Revelation shows Christ leading heaven's armies to execute that judgment — the final reckoning that vindicates God's justice.
prophecies.explanationZh: 约珥与但以理都预言列国受审之日。马太描写万民被聚集审判。弥赛亚以公义法官面貌临到时，列国要受审判。

interpretations.note: Destruction of nations by Israel in Messianic days (Bemidbar R.)

prophecies.title: Final Battle
prophecies.otText: I will turn you around and drag you along. I will bring you from the far north and send you against the mountains of Israel.
prophecies.otTextZh: 我必调转你，领你前往，使你从北方的极处上来，带你到以色列的山上。
prophecies.ntText: When the thousand years are over, Satan will be released from his prison and will go out to deceive the nations in the four corners of the earth — Gog and Magog.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 出来要迷惑地上四方（原文是角）的列国，就是歌革和玛各，叫他们聚集争战。他们的人数多如海沙。
prophecies.explanation: Ezekiel prophesied a final gathering of hostile nations against God's people. Revelation identifies this as the last battle — Gog and Magog deceived by Satan, ultimately destroyed by God's fire.
prophecies.explanationZh: 启示录所写的哈米吉多顿与旧约末日争战呼应。弥赛亚作得胜的王终结历史性的争战。最终的和平非靠军力、而是借弥赛亚的得胜而来。

interpretations.note: Bemidbar R. 13 — Messianic battle with Gog and Magog

prophecies.title: River of Life
prophecies.otText: Swarms of living creatures will live wherever the river flows. There will be large numbers of fish, because this water flows there and makes the salt water fresh; so where the river flows everything will live.
prophecies.otTextZh: 这河水所到之处，凡滋生的动物都必生活，并且因这流来的水必有极多的鱼，海水也变甜了。这河水所到之处，百物都必生活。
prophecies.ntText: On each side of the river stood the tree of life, bearing twelve crops of fruit, yielding its fruit every month. And the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 在河这边与那边有生命树，结十二样（或译：回）果子，每月都结果子；树上的叶子乃为医治万民。
prophecies.explanation: Ezekiel saw a river flowing from the temple, bringing life wherever it flowed. Revelation shows this river in the new Jerusalem — the river of life with the tree of life healing the nations. What Ezekiel glimpsed, Christ fulfills.
prophecies.explanationZh: 以西结与启示录都描写从宝座流出的生命河。耶稣也发出「活水江河」的应许。弥赛亚的国度中生命之水源源不断供给万民。

interpretations.note: Shem. R. 15 — living waters and healing trees in Messianic era

prophecies.title: Two Thrones
prophecies.otText: As I looked, thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days took his seat. His clothing was as white as snow; the hair of his head was white like wool.
prophecies.otTextZh: 我观看，见有宝座设立，上头坐著亘古常在者。他的衣服洁白如雪，头发如纯净的羊毛。宝座乃火焰，其轮乃烈火。
prophecies.ntText: To the one who is victorious, I will give the right to sit with me on my throne, just as I was victorious and sat down with my Father on his throne.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 得胜的，我要赐他在我宝座上与我同坐，就如我得了胜，在我父的宝座上与他同坐一般。
prophecies.explanation: Daniel saw thrones set in place before the Ancient of Days. Jesus promises to share His throne with those who overcome — the heavenly enthronement Daniel witnessed includes a seat for every faithful believer.
prophecies.explanationZh: 启示录描写神与羔羊共享宝座。这呼应「神与基督一同坐席作王」的圣经图画。弥赛亚与父神同尊、同荣、同掌权。

interpretations.note: R. Akiba — two thrones: one for God

prophecies.title: Seventy Weeks
prophecies.otText: Seventy 'sevens' are decreed for your people and your holy city to finish transgression, to put an end to sin, to atone for wickedness, to bring in everlasting righteousness.
prophecies.otTextZh: 「为你本国之民和你圣城，已经定了七十个七。要止住罪过，除净罪恶，赎尽罪孽，引进（或译：彰显）永义，封住异象和预言，并膏至圣者（者：或译所）。
prophecies.ntText: They will fall by the sword and will be taken as prisoners to all the nations. Jerusalem will be trampled on by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
prophecies.ntTextZh: 他们要倒在刀下，又被掳到各国去。耶路撒冷要被外邦人践踏，直到外邦人的日期满了。」
prophecies.explanation: Daniel received God's precise timeline for finishing transgression and bringing everlasting righteousness. Jesus pointed to Jerusalem's fate as part of this prophetic clock — the times of the Gentiles marking the countdown to His return.
prophecies.explanationZh: 但以理的七十个七预言弥赛亚「受膏、被剪除」的时刻。这建立对弥赛亚来临的时间框架。历代解释虽有差异，皆指弥赛亚的来临与被剪除为历史的分水岭。

interpretations.note: Naz. 32b — seventy weeks until second Temple destroyed; Messianic timing

prophecies.title: Great Tribulation
prophecies.otText: At that time Michael, the great prince who protects your people, will arise. There will be a time of distress such as has not happened from the beginning of nations until then.
